hep-ph.abstract: Over the past couple of decades, the Liquid Scintillator Neutrino Detector (LSND) and MiniBooNE (MB) neutrino experiments have provided statistically significant evidence of persistent and as yet unexplained electron-like event excesses. The MicroBooNE experiment, with sensitive particle identification capabilities designed to shed light on these anomalous results, has conducted a number of analyses to test whether the excess is due to photons, electrons or $e^+e^-$ pair productions, all of which give almost identical signals in LSND and MB. Recent MicroBooNE searches, in addition to checking Standard Model (SM) processes, have focused on proposed new physics scenarios involving new mediators and dark portals beyond the SM. We study the consequences and effects of these analyses for the many theoretical proposals put forth to generate the three types of signals above in order to understand the observed excesses. We discuss which classes of solutions are allowed, disallowed or require further scrutiny involving theoretical and experimental efforts. We give an example of a new solution that survives the restrictions imposed by MicroBooNE results and other existing bounds. We point out that a light ($m\leq 30$ MeV) dark neutral spin zero mediator with dominantly pseudoscalar couplings, decaying to an $e^+e^-$ pair, can account for the observations. We indicate that if such a model is realised, it may point to the possibility that neutrinos are Dirac particles, and that there are dark Heavy Neutral Leptons (HNLs) of mass ${\cal O}(100)$ MeV. We discuss issues related to CP violation and ultra-violet completion of these models. Finally we stress that a search for the excess in incoherent scattering channels in MicroBooNE and SBND could help clarify the physics behind these persistent anomalies.

hep-ph.title: Dark Matter Stability from residual flavour symmetries
hep-ph.author: Giacomo Landini, Simone Marciano, Federico Mescia
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a model-independent framework in which Dark Matter stability emerges naturally from residual discrete $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries left unbroken by the spontaneous breaking of continuous flavour symmetries, both Abelian and non-Abelian. No ad hoc stabilizing symmetry is required, as Dark Matter stability is an inherent consequence of the underlying flavour dynamics. As an explicit example, we construct a prototype model based on a $\text{SU}(2)_\text{F} \otimes \text{U}(1)_\text{F}$ Froggatt-Nielsen symmetry, which successfully reproduces the observed charged lepton mass spectrum and the PMNS mixing matrix, while identifying the lightest sterile neutrino as a stable Dark Matter candidate. Furthermore, we study the Dark Matter phenomenology within our model in the freeze-in regime, including production channels mediated by higher-dimensional operators suppressed by the cutoff scale $\Lambda$. Our analysis shows that continuous flavour symmetries can provide a unified, self-consistent framework addressing both the flavour puzzle and the origin, stability, and production of Dark Matter.

hep-ph.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
hep-ph.author: Sarah R. Geller, Sol Gutierrez-Lara, David I. Kaiser, Thomas Steingasser
hep-ph.abstract: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential. After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.

hep-ph.title: What Do Event Generators Compute? Flux Functionals from Detector Operators
hep-ph.author: Jack Holguin
hep-ph.abstract: Every physical prediction of an event generator is a statement about the hadronic fluxes that can be recorded by particle detectors. By contrast, the formal backbone of modern event-generator precision is provided by the unobservable partonic final states of the parton shower, with hadronisation included as a model. We construct the probability distribution of the hadronic fluxes non-perturbatively, directly from detector operators acting on asymptotic hadronic states, and encode it in an event generator source functional. This distribution contains every measurement a detector can make, and is therefore what a generator must compute with precision, including the effects of hadronisation. Restricting the functional to the energy flow yields the parton shower source functional, which is infrared and collinear safe and contains every calorimetric observable, making it a natural object against which to assess parton-shower accuracy. We compute its logarithmic structure at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, finding it directly sensitive to kinematic recoil and hence to the recoil scheme of a parton shower. The parton shower functional depends on a continuum of low scales, one for each resolved direction, and in a toy model its logarithms cannot be entirely resummed within a factorisation whose evolution derives only from the high-scale physics. Our operator-based formulation opens the door to the study of event-generator-like systems in theories beyond QCD, including conformal theories such as $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and thereby offers a new route to non-perturbative insight into event generation.

hep-ph.title: Neutrino Tridents and $W$-boson production at the Muon Collider
hep-ph.author: Felix Kling, Toni Mäkelä, Sebastian Trojanowski, Bei Zhou
hep-ph.abstract: Muon colliders are exceptionally intense sources of multi-TeV neutrinos, allowing even relatively small detectors to record large rates of neutrino interactions. In addition to serving as neutrino-ion collider for precision measurements of neutrino deep inelastic scattering, this setup allow to study even rare neutrino processes with at high statistics. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of measuring neutrino trident and on-shell W-boson production, predicting over one million trident events and one hundred thousand W-boson events in a 100 kg silicon-based active target over ten years and allowing to detect these processes for the first time. We further show that these measurements could constrain new vector and axial-vector interactions beyond projected DUNE sensitivities and provide unprecedented constraints on the high-x photon distribution through W-boson production near threshold. We also discuss strategies for signal-background discrimination and the resulting detector requirements.

hep-ph.title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
hep-ph.author: Yu-Chen Hu, Cong-Cong Ye, Craig D. Roberts, Zhao-Qian Yao
hep-ph.abstract: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $\tau$ and $\mu$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8\sigma$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3\sigma$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.

hep-ph.title: Non-accumulation of background-enhanced neutrino forces in proto-neutron stars
hep-ph.author: Himanshu Bora, Anupam Deka, Debajyoti Dutta
hep-ph.abstract: In a neutrino background, the vacuum two-neutrino exchange potential $V \propto G_F^2 /r^5$ acts as a much longer-ranged interaction, scaling as $V\sim1/r$ for a directional background. A proto-neutron star (PNS) hosts one of the densest astrophysical neutrino environments known, and naturally provides a setting in which to test whether this pairwise enhancement produces a macroscopic Hartree contribution. We show that this does not happen. In the spin-independent sector, averaging over pair orientations projects the background onto its angular monopole. The bulk Hartree contribution then saturates instead of growing with system size. We also find that the spin-dependent parity-conserving and parity-violating terms do not generate macroscopic growth under the PNS mean-field conditions considered here. Thus, although the pair potential can be strongly enhanced, the resulting bulk interaction remains very small. The suppression comes from the angular and oscillatory structure of the kernel, not from screening. Within the Standard Model mechanism considered here, the effect is not important for the PNS equation of state or for events like pulsar kicks.

hep-ph.title: QGrAT: Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer for Jet Tagging
hep-ph.author: Pallavi Bhardwaj, Michael Spannowsky
hep-ph.abstract: Lorentz symmetry and the three-prong structure of hadronic top decays provide physical guidance for designing compact quantum jet taggers. We introduce QGrAT (Quantum Grade-Aware Transformer), a quantum transformer that incorporates these structures into its interactions between constituent qubits. Geometric features constructed from the constituent four-momenta are organised by the grades of the spacetime Clifford algebra $C\ell(1,3)$, and their grade-specific inner products determine the pairwise attention couplings. For fixed constituents and co-transforming reference vectors, these couplings are Lorentz invariant, although the component-wise input encoding makes the complete classifier frame dependent. An auxiliary qubit introduces an explicit three-particle interaction through products of pairwise Minkowski inner products, while a trainable in-circuit readout converts the resulting quantum state into a classification score. We evaluate the architecture in state-vector simulation on the Top Tagging benchmarks. With ten constituents per jet, the configuration using grades $0\text{-}3$ and the three-particle ancilla requires twelve qubits and $144$ trainable parameters, reaching AUC $0.944 \pm 0.002$ and background rejection $1/\varepsilon_B = 35.7 \pm 2.4\ (96.8 \pm 7.7)$ at signal efficiency $\varepsilon_S = 0.50\ (0.30)$. This performance is competitive with the L-GATr-Slim baseline at matched constituent and parameter budgets. Adding the three-particle ancilla raises background rejection at $50\%$ signal efficiency from $19.9$ to $35.7$, whereas extending the representation to the tested grade-$4$ feature gives no consistent improvement. The study establishes a framework for incorporating spacetime geometry into quantum attention and identifies explicit three-particle correlations as the principal source of improved background rejection among the architectural variations tested.

hep-ph.title: Parton and nuclear dynamics at large $x$: the CJ26 global QCD analysis
hep-ph.author: Alberto Accardi, Matteo Cerutti, Cynthia E. Keppel, Shujie Li, J. F. Owens, Sanghwa Park, Peter Risse
hep-ph.abstract: We present the new CTEQ-JLab global QCD analysis, called CJ26, that simultaneously fits parton distribution functions of the proton and nuclear effects in deuteron targets. This work includes, for the first time in a global fit, the full set of JLab 6 GeV inclusive DIS measurements and the first published JLab 12 GeV data. The analysis focuses on the large-$x$ region, and carefully treats the interplay between higher-twist effects and off-shell corrections in low-energy proton and deuteron target data. We discuss their effect on quark and gluon distributions, and highlight the importance of quantifying the experimental correlated systematic uncertainty to achieve fits of the highest accuracy. We also outline how upcoming data may help unravel the nuclear and partonic dynamics in light nuclei. The extracted next-to-leading order parton distributions are available on the CJ web pages in LHAPDF format for general use, accompanied by leading- and higher-twist structure functions calculated with the simultaneously fitted PDFs, higher-twist corrections, and off-shell corrections. This write up clarifies several points that became clearer while finalizing the CJ26 paper and can be read as a companion to the latter.

hep-ph.title: Kernel moments and thermodynamic stability in nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio models
hep-ph.author: Xiaozhu Yu, Xinyang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We study thermodynamic consistency and stability in a covariant two-flavor nonlocal Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model at zero chemical potential in the homogeneous quark mean-field approximation. A controlled large-source expansion gives a sufficient entropy-sign criterion directly from Euclidean kernel moments, without locating propagator poles. At fixed couplings and kernel, every admissible positive Gaussian mixture develops negative total entropy at sufficiently large source mass for each fixed positive temperature. In a separate light-source fit to pion observables and a subtracted condensate, one quartic-exponent kernel has positive entropy and heat capacity for all $T>0$, while $dP/d\epsilon=s/C_V$ exceeds unity on a finite interval. This constructive example separates thermal positivity from the static EOS slope test. Numerical refits show that the enhancement weakens with the condensate input, and a certified counterexample excludes uniform thermal positivity over the adopted matching domain. The results provide diagnostics of the mean-field functional, rather than a preferred phenomenological kernel. Omitted thermal mesons can change the low-temperature slope test, and the static derivative does not determine a real-time front velocity.

hep-ph.title: Octupole parton structure of spin-3/2 targets
hep-ph.author: Brandon B. Le, Dustin Keller
hep-ph.abstract: In spin-$3/2$ targets, octupole polarization can reveal quark and gluon correlations beyond those probed by vector polarization and quadrupole alignment. Here, we construct the complete leading-twist gluon transverse-momentum-dependent distribution basis, with 32 independent coefficients for each specified Wilson-line and color structure. Fourteen of these describe octupole dependence in gluon number, helicity, and linear polarization. In heavy-quark-pair leptoproduction at small, nonzero pair imbalance, comparing target states with opposite octupoles and identical lower moments isolates the octupole contribution. Beam-helicity reversal and joint angular projections in target orientation and pair-imbalance azimuth can then separate all fourteen gluon octupole responses at leading-power Born order. We also derive the incoming-target quark responses in semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan production. Time-reversal relations between distributions remain valid under symmetry-preserving renormalization and evolution, while predictions across processes require factorization formulas connecting those distributions to scattering observables. Finally, we connect this framework to polarized $^{7}$Li through its collinear limits and nuclear spin-orbital correlations.

hep-ph.title: A mechanism of the power-counting breaking in chiral perturbation theory
hep-ph.author: Ming-Ze Ma, Shao-Zhou Jiang
hep-ph.abstract: Chiral perturbation theory is a power tool for studying the low-energy strong interactions. In the conventional chiral expansion, according to the power counting rule, the higher-order corrections for physical observables are expected to decrease order by order as the chiral dimension increases. However, most previous study of $\pi K$ scattering lengths by different references showed that the $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ correction to the scattering lengths is anomalously large and even exceeds the $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$ one. It poses a serious challenge to the convergence of chiral expansion. In order to explore the underlying origin of this phenomenon, the contributions of two-loop diagrams, one-loop diagrams and tree diagrams for the $\pi K$ scattering amplitude are detailed analyzed. The reducible two-loop integrals, sunset integrals and vertex integrals from the $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$ order all violate the power counting rule. The sunset and vertex integrals can be largely canceled numerically, but not enough. Furthermore, $\pi K$ scattering is compared with $\pi\pi$ scattering, which seems not violate the power counting rule. The analysis indicates that $\pi\pi$ scattering contains a higher symmetry, although each $\mathcal{O}(p^6)$-order part also violates the power counting rule, but the violation is much smaller than the one from $\pi K$ scattering. Large kaon mass also makes a contribution to the power-counting breaking, but it is not a major origin. Hence, it needs to pay more attention to the many-loop low-symmetry diagrams in future work. These diagrams may give large contribution and cannot be ignored.

hep-ph.title: Heavy flavour production in the presence of a weak magnetic field
hep-ph.author: Sudeep Saha, Sandeep Chatterjee, Ujjal Kumar Dey, Snigdh Ghosh
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate analytic expression for the cross section up to order $(eB)^2$ for the production of a heavy quark $(Q)$ of mass $m_Q$ through the gluon $(g)$ fusion process $g+g\to Q+\bar{Q}$ in the presence of a constant weak external magnetic field $(B)$ with strength $eB \ll m_Q^2$. This is done using the weak-field expansion of the fermion propagator calculated within Schwinger's proper-time formalism. Owing to the hierarchy of scales ($m_Q^2 \gg eB$), we neglect the effects of the magnetic field on the quark and antiquark spinors in the external lines. Since the magnetic field breaks rotational invariance, the cross section becomes anisotropic and depends on the relative orientation angle $(\theta)$ between the magnetic field and the incoming gluons in the center-of-mass frame. The lowest-order magnetic correction to the vacuum cross section scales as $(eB)^2$ and is found to have $\cos 2\theta$ and $\cos 4\theta$ dependence, reflecting the breaking of rotational symmetry by the magnetic field. The cross section is maximized when the gluons propagate along the field direction ($\theta = 0, \pi$) and minimized in the perpendicular configuration ($\theta = \pi/2$). The resulting asymmetry peaks near the production threshold and falls with increasing center-of-mass energy, scaling as $(eB)^2/m_Q^4$ with the quark mass. These results provide direct, calculable signatures of the initial-stage magnetic field in relativistic heavy-ion collisions which can, in principle, be imprinted on heavy-flavour observables measured in the final state of heavy-ion collisions.

hep-ph.title: One-loop contributing for $A \rightarrow Z Z γ$ in the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model with Vector-Like Quarks
hep-ph.author: Dzung Tri Tran(HCMUS, DTU), Vo Quoc Phong(HCMUS), Khiem Hong Phan(EIU)
hep-ph.abstract: In this paper, we present the first results for the one-loop decay $A \rightarrow ZZ\gamma$ in the Two-Higgs-Doublet Model and its extension with Vector-Like Quarks. We calculate the one-loop partial decay widths and branching ratios for both unpolarized and polarized final-state $Z$ bosons. The effects of Vector-Like Quarks propagating in the loop are also examined in our phenomenological analysis. We find that the branching ratios can reach $10^{-5}-10^{-4}$ for several benchmark points within the viable parameter space of the considered models. The contributions from Vector-Like Quarks can modify the total rates by approximately $5\%$. With the high luminosities expected at future multi-TeV muon colliders, these effects may be experimentally accessible.

hep-ph.title: Covariant approach to allowed beta decay
hep-ph.author: Sergio Cruz-Alzaga, Adam Falkowski
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a Lorentz-covariant on-shell formalism for allowed nuclear beta decay. Nuclear matrix elements are organized in a systematic effective field theory expansion in the recoil momentum, with the dependence on nuclear spin and polarization encoded in little-group-covariant structures. In this language, we construct the most general standard and exotic currents for allowed transitions through first recoil order. We then derive the differential decay distribution encoded in a set of Lorentz-invariant form factors. Specializing to the rest frame of the parent nucleus, we relate our parameters to those used in the traditional beta-decay literature and in nucleon- and quark-level effective field theories. The formalism provides a natural framework for extensions to higher recoil orders, radiative corrections, and forbidden transitions.

hep-ph.title: Color Lorentz force on a transversely polarized quark in the nucleon
hep-ph.author: Ziqi Zhang, Chandan Mondal, Siqi Xu, Xingbo Zhao, James P. Vary
hep-ph.abstract: The $x^2$ moment of the genuine twist-3 component of the unpolarized scalar parton distribution function $e(x)$ is related to the average transverse color Lorentz force experienced by a transversely polarized quark in an unpolarized nucleon. This higher-twist quantity probes quark--gluon correlations and provides unique insight into the nonperturbative dynamics of quantum chromodynamics. For the first time, we study the corresponding off-forward matrix element and derive its Lorentz-covariant decomposition in terms of generalized form factors. We calculate these form factors from light-front wave functions obtained by solving the light-front Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework. Their Fourier transforms provide a spatial picture of the transverse color forces in impact-parameter space. In particular, $\mathscr{F}_2$, whose forward limit is directly related to the twist-3 matrix element $e_2$, can be interpreted as the impact-parameter-space representation of the Boer--Mulders force, providing an intuitive spatial picture of the final-state interaction mechanism underlying the Boer--Mulders effect.

hep-ph.title: Signature of GW from the Hidden Sector in light of the Recent LZ Event
hep-ph.author: Sujit Kumar Sahoo, Narendra Sahu, Vicky Singh Thounaojam
hep-ph.abstract: The LZ collaboration has recently reported a single nuclear-recoil event at $E_R=248\pm23_\text{stat}\pm23_\text{sys}$ keV, observed in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure with a local significance of $3.4\sigma$, pointing towards an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation. We explain this event within a gauged $U(1)_X$ hidden-sector model, spontaneously broken by a singlet scalar whose vacuum expectation value (VEV) gives rise to: \textit{(i)} gauge boson mass, \textit{(ii)} a small Majorana mass for the vector-like singlet fermion, the DM candidate, charged under the new symmetry, which splits the fermion into two pseudo-Dirac states (mass splitting proportional to the scalar VEV) thus resulting in a purely off-diagonal vector current, \textit{(iii)} the frequency and the amplitude of the GW signal arising from the hidden sector symmetry breaking via first-order phase transition (FOPT). The symmetry-breaking scale thus provides a multi-messenger probe connecting terrestrial direct-detection kinematics at the LZ and early-universe FOPT thermodynamics while obtaining thermal DM relic abundance. We delineate the viable parameter space compatible with the LZ event, correct relic density, and detectable GW signals in the low frequency regimes at future interferometers like $\mu {\rm ARES}$ and THEIA while satisfying existing cosmological, astrophysical, and terrestrial bounds.

hep-ph.title: Cosmological Consequences of a Highly Decoupled Right-handed Neutrino
hep-ph.author: Stephen F. King, Rishav Roshan, Sudipta Show
hep-ph.abstract: In the minimal type-I seesaw, one right-handed neutrino (RHN) can decouple from neutrino mass generation. Such a state is usually neglected, yet its feeble couplings make it long-lived, and it can dominate the energy density of the Universe before decaying. We study this in a minimal $U(1)_{B-L}$ model, where the RHNs are produced through $B-L$ gauge interactions, for the cases of a decoupled lightest RHN $N_1$ and a decoupled heaviest RHN $N_3$. The resulting early matter-dominated era dilutes the baryon asymmetry, and for decoupled $N_3$ it also delays the equilibration of the charged-lepton Yukawa interactions, allowing a lighter $N_1$ to generate the asymmetry in the unflavoured regime. Breaking $U(1)_{B-L}$ forms cosmic strings whose gravitational-wave background acquires a spectral break from the early matter-dominated era, with a frequency set by the decoupled RHN mass and the lightest neutrino mass, within reach of future detectors such as SKA, THEIA, LISA, $\mu$ARES, DECIGO and ET.

hep-ph.title: HEPTABench: A framework for portable and controlled agentic evaluations in high energy physics
hep-ph.author: Tony Menzo, Alexander Roman, George T. Fleming, Sergei Gleyzer, Konstantin Matchev, Stephen Mrenna
hep-ph.abstract: Quantifying the capability and reliability of agentic systems in high-energy physics (HEP) requires repeated evaluations under controlled configurations. Establishing whether changes to models, tools, or harnesses improve performance also requires these components to be varied independently. We present the High Energy Physics Tool-and-Agent Benchmarking (HEPTABench) framework for portable and controlled evaluations of agentic systems, with separately configurable tasks, scaffolding, models, providers, harnesses, and domain capabilities. The framework combines HEP benchmark tasks and scientific rubrics with experiment execution and versioned tool interfaces. To support inspection, reproducibility, and post-hoc grading, the framework prioritizes recording and reporting complete experiment specifications, agent trajectories, and experiment artifacts. We demonstrate the framework in two benchmark campaigns. The first campaign evaluates a forward long-lived-particle reach calculation across four frontier coding-agent systems, comparing their built-in coding tools with the same tools supplemented by HEP domain tools. We show that including these HEP domain tools improves numerical accuracy and reduces trial-to-trial dispersion for every tested system. In a complementary campaign covering eight symbolic two-body decay tasks, we show that adding symbolic domain tools increases the fraction of successful trials for Claude Haiku 4.5 from $8\%$ to $79\%$, while GPT-5.5 succeeds in every trial with built-in tools alone. Through systematic evaluation of agentic systems, HEPTABench enables the identification of factors that improve the accuracy and reliability of their scientific work.

hep-ph.title: Deviations to cobimaximal mixing in a 3+1 neutrino scenario
hep-ph.author: Diana C. Rivera-Agudelo, S. L. Tostado
hep-ph.abstract: Cobimaximal mixing remains a viable approximate pattern since the predicted atmospheric angle ($\pi/4$) and Dirac CP phase ($-\pi/2$) are compatible with current experimental data at the $3\sigma$ level. In this work, we investigate how an additional sterile neutrino state breaks the cobimaximal mixing and the underlying $\mu-\tau$ reflection symmetry in a $3+1$ neutrino scenario. Given the strong constraints already imposed on active-sterile mixings, we examine the resulting restrictions on the model parameter space, assuming a small symmetry breaking induced by the sterile state. We derive predictions for the relevant model parameters, active-sterile mixing angles, and Dirac CP-violating phases, by considering small deviations from the symmetric limit. We also analyze the allowed combinations of Majorana phases through their impact on the effective Majorana mass governing neutrinoless double beta decay. Current experimental limits on this process impose severe constraints on the inverted ordering realization of the $3+1$ scenario, excluding the small breaking regime within the parameter ranges considered. In contrast, the normal ordering case remains viable and predicts values of the effective Majorana mass that lie within the sensitivity reach of upcoming neutrinoless double beta decay experiments.

hep-ph.title: Multiboson production at multi-TeV lepton colliders as complementary probes to rare Higgs decays
hep-ph.author: Dario Buttazzo, Keshav Chaudhary, Roberto Franceschini, Arman Korajac
hep-ph.abstract: We study the potential of very high-energy lepton colliders to probe effective operators affecting the loop-induced Higgs boson decays $h\to \gamma\gamma$ and $h\to Z\gamma$, providing constraints complementary to Higgs coupling measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. In particular, we consider processes with two and three bosons in the final state and analyze their individual and combined impact on the effective field theory parameter space. We demonstrate that these processes at a multi-TeV lepton collider can improve the bounds from rare Higgs decays and electroweak precision observables, surpassing the projections for High-Luminosity LHC and FCC-ee. This is especially true for triboson processes, whose sensitivity is enhanced by the growth with energy of the new physics cross-sections, making them the dominant constraint at very high energies, potentially competitive with FCC-hh.

hep-ph.title: Virtual photon bremsstrahlung in a magnetized quark-gluon-plasma
hep-ph.author: Aritra Bandyopadhyay, Krzysztof Redlich, Chihiro Sasaki
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate dilepton production via virtual quark bremsstrahlung in a hot, magnetized quark-gluon plasma (QGP), extending the Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal (LPM) framework to account for a background magnetic field and for Fermi-Dirac quark statistics. An external electromagnetic field drives the quark distribution out of equilibrium, and this off-equilibrium correction, obtained from the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation, is in principle explicit in the electric and magnetic field strengths. We argue that this correction, being linear in the electric field, vanishes identically upon integration over the full dilepton solid angle and therefore does not contribute to the dilepton production rate (DPR). The leading magnetic-field signature in the rate instead enters entirely through the equilibrium sector: the medium density and Debye screening mass, computed from the Landau-level structure of the magnetized QGP, modifying the LPM suppression parameter. Working in the regime relevant to the hydrodynamic phase of heavy-ion collisions, we present the LPM-induced DPR for quark scatterers and establish, for the first time, a nonzero magnetic-field imprint on this observable through the LPM mechanism.

hep-ph.title: Comment on arXiv:2510.21705 "Fundamental Impossibility of a Superradiant Neutrino Laser" and comment on arXiv:2510.21692 "Can Bose-Einstein Condensates Enhance Radioactive Decay?"
hep-ph.author: Ralph G. DeVoe
hep-ph.abstract: We show that the small value of the neutrino cross-section rules out superradiance in the laboratory.

hep-ph.title: An All-Sky Search for Moving Gamma-Ray Sources with Fermi-LAT
hep-ph.author: Dou Lai, James Unwin
hep-ph.abstract: Nearby compact gamma-ray sources can move appreciably during the Fermi-LAT mission and thus evade searches that assume a stationary sky. Compact dark matter halos, dark matter spikes around primordial black holes (PBH), and evaporating PBH provide potential examples. We perform a novel all-sky search for steady point sources moving at 0.25 deg/yr-0.8deg/yr in ten years of 1-100 GeV Fermi-LAT data. For a transverse speed of 200 km/s, this angular range probes distances of roughly $3.0\times10^3$ AU to $9.7\times10^3$ AU. We find 577 candidate tracks, consistent with $533\pm27.0$ tracks in time-scrambled skies. We place a model-independent 90% upper limit of 80.8 recovered signal tracks. At peak calibrated sensitivity, this corresponds to fewer than 123 steady, full-sky sources with an incident $E^{-2}$ photon spectrum. We give the calibrated detection efficiency of the search to steady point sources and use it to derive illustrative constraints on both evaporating PBHs and PBHs surrounded by annihilating dark matter halos.

hep-ph.title: Ultralight scalars and invisible gravitons
hep-ph.author: Massimo Giovannini
hep-ph.abstract: Unless the tensor to scalar ratio is small enough, the non-adiabatic mode associated with the ultralight bosons may be dangerously comparable with the adiabatic spectrum of curvature inhomogeneities. We point out here that this statement depends on the timeline of the post-inflationary expansion rate. Provided the decelerated evolution is slower than radiation for a sufficiently long period, the relative weight of the non-adiabatic and adiabatic components does not conflict with the direct constraints coming from the large-scale observations. Conversely the presence of ultralight bosons excludes the presence of long stages expanding faster than radiation. The synthesis of the light nuclei and the spectrum of the relic gravitons at high frequencies set the relevant constraints on the duration of the decelerated stages, on the delayed dominance of radiation and on the mass range of the ultralight scalars.

hep-ph.title: IceCube data for astrophysical neutrinos exhibit q-statistical behavior
hep-ph.author: Constantino Tsallis, Ugur Tirnakli
hep-ph.abstract: Relevant IceCube recent data for astrophysical neutrinos are analyzed. Similarly to cosmic rays and proton-proton LHC collisions, the corresponding spectra are satisfactorily described, for the entire interval of measured energies, through q-Gaussians. This fact reinforces the already available evidence that nonadditive entropies (either of the $S_q$ class or of the $S_{delta}$ one, or even alternative ones) appear to play a crucial role in systems such as black holes and related cosmological phenomena (e.g., dark energy). The IceCube data yield sensibly high values for the momenta-distribution nonadditive index (q \simeq 1.6), in contrast with the cosmic rays values (q \simeq 1.2) and the LHC values (q \simeq 1.1). This fact neatly indicates very-long-ranged space-time correlations. The detailed associated physical mechanisms remain, at the present stage, as an instigating open issue.

hep-ph.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
hep-ph.author: Jintao Zou, Zizhuo Zhao, Yongtao Jia, Ligong Bian
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength. The lifetime of the sound wave source increases with decreasing $\alpha$: for weaker transitions the source can persist for longer than a Hubble time, while for stronger transitions it decays within a Hubble time. When the walls propagate as deflagrations, the GW spectral shape changes drastically, with steeper ultraviolet tails and a shorter-lived sound wave source. We also observe that the magnitude of the normalized GWs is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than obtained in the Minkowski spacetime simulations.

hep-ph.title: On some nonlinear extensions to Maxwell's electrodynamics
hep-ph.author: Bertrand Berche, Ernesto Medina
hep-ph.abstract: Soon after Maxwell's celebrated synthesis of electrodynamics, the discovery of the electron raised fundamental questions about the nature and structure of elementary particles. The picture of a small, rigid, charged body of finite radius faced the difficulty of introducing non-electromagnetic forces or stresses to prevent the charge from dispersing, an assumption that was increasingly regarded as unsatisfactory. The alternative description in terms of a point charge was no more satisfactory, because its electromagnetic self-energy diverges. From the early twentieth century onward, several authors therefore explored modifications of Maxwell's theory, with nonlinear electrodynamics emerging as a particularly natural and radical possibility. In this paper, we revisit at the undergraduate level some of the nonlinear theories proposed in this context and explore their ability to address the classical self-energy problem of charged particles.

hep-ph.title: Primordial Graviton Entanglement in Quasicrystalline Inflation
hep-ph.author: Jiro Soda
hep-ph.abstract: We study the entanglement structure of gravitons in quasicrystalline inflation. Both parity-even and parity-odd interactions generate graviton pairs with nonzero total momentum. For opposite-helicity pairs with identical momenta, the parity-even contribution can be nonzero, whereas the parity-odd contribution vanishes. The transition from inflation to radiation domination produces additional conventional two-mode squeezing. We derive the resulting normal and anomalous covariances. The initially nonzero reciprocal blocks of the full field-momentum covariance remain nonzero under homogeneous evolution, although individual components can vanish. We show that this homogeneous, helicity-preserving evolution acts unitarily within each helicity sector and therefore preserves the entanglement between the complete right- and left-helicity sectors. Nevertheless, it can eliminate entanglement in the reduced state of a co-propagating pair. We illustrate this distinction using a solvable four-mode model.

hep-ph.title: Joint Constraints on the Hubble Constant and Cosmic Baryon Density from Localized Fast Radio Bursts and DESI DR2 Baryon Acoustic Oscillations
hep-ph.author: Ji-Guo Zhang, Tian-Nuo Li, Guo-Hong Du, Wan-Peng Sun, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) probe free-electron columns along cosmological sightlines through their dispersion measures (DMs), whereas baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) constrain cosmic expansion geometry through acoustic distance ratios. In this work, we leverage their distinct physical sensitivities to simultaneously determine the Hubble constant ($H_0$) and cosmic baryon density ($\Omega_{\rm b}$) without external cosmic microwave background (CMB) or Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) priors. Combining 120 localized FRBs and DESI DR2 BAO, we obtain $H_0=71.4^{+2.2}_{-2.5}\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}=0.0503^{+0.0025}_{-0.0021}$ in $\Lambda$CDM, corresponding to precisions of $3.3\%$ and $4.6\%$, respectively. The inferred $H_0$ is statistically consistent with both SH0ES and CMB, and $\Omega_{\rm b}$ agrees with the joint constraint from BBN and CMB. Adopting IllustrisTNG-based DM distributions and fixing the diffuse-gas baryon fraction tightens the constraint to $H_0=68.8\pm1.0\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}\ Mpc^{-1}}$, but lowers the central value toward the CMB-inferred value, identifying extragalactic DM modeling as the dominant systematic uncertainty. These results establish FRB-BAO complementarity as a new avenue for simultaneously constraining $H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}$.

hep-ph.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $ϕ^4$ lattice models
hep-ph.author: Adith A, A. Bhagwat
hep-ph.abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

hep-ph.title: Bayesian exploration of weakly interacting models of dark matter admixed neutron stars based on multi-density constraints
hep-ph.author: Payaswinee Arvikar, Prashant Thakur, Sarmistha Banik
hep-ph.abstract: We present a unified Bayesian analysis of Higgs-portal, neutron-decay, and axion-like-particle (ALP)-mediated dark matter in neutron stars within the single-fluid approximation. Using a common relativistic mean-field description of hadronic matter, we combine finite-nucleus and heavy-ion collision data, chiral effective field theory, NICER measurements of four pulsars, and GW170817. The individual dark-sector parameters remain weakly determined, while model-dependent shifts in nuclear skewness reveal the sensitivity of the inferred hadronic equation of state to the assumed dark-matter mechanism. The three scenarios yield substantially overlapping mass-radius and tidal-deformability predictions, with median maximum masses near $2.1\,M_\odot$. For $1.4\,M_\odot$ stars, the Higgs-portal model predicts higher $f$-mode frequencies and shorter damping times than the neutron-decay and ALP models, although their credible regions overlap. Comparison with three consistently reanalysed two-fluid models gives the largest Bayesian evidence to neutron decay: under the adopted priors, its Bayes factors relative to the Higgs-portal and two-fluid alternatives are approximately $24$-$37$, but only $2.2$ relative to ALP. This ranking concerns complete dark-matter models and does not establish a general preference for either fluid description or evidence for a dark component itself. Improved nuclear constraints and future gravitational-wave asteroseismology could provide complementary information to disentangle the hadronic and dark-sector contributions.

hep-ph.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
hep-ph.author: Yoritaka Iwata, Yasuhiro Takei
hep-ph.abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll \phi_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > \phi_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle \phi \rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(\phi) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

hep-ph.title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
hep-ph.author: ZiHao Liu, Mei Huang
hep-ph.abstract: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

hep-ph.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
hep-ph.author: Stéphane Fay, Mikel Artola, Leandros Perivolaropoulos
hep-ph.abstract: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $\eta(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = \alpha{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $\Lambda$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $\Lambda$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $\Omega_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $\eta(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $\eta(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $\alpha \simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.

hep-ph.title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
hep-ph.author: Guangshang Chen, Jianpeng Dai, Yang Xiao
hep-ph.abstract: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

hep-ph.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
hep-ph.author: Paul H Frampton
hep-ph.abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

hep-ph.title: Impact of Window Observables on the Transversity Quark Parton Distribution Function
hep-ph.author: Daniel Adamiak, Christopher Monahan
hep-ph.abstract: We study the potential impact of lattice QCD window observables on nucleon isovector quark transversity parton distribution functions (PDFs) using the ePump Hessian-updating framework. Window observables, recently proposed inarXiv:2505.22795as benchmark quantities enabling direct quantitative comparison between lattice QCD and phenomenological PDF extractions, are weighted integrals of PDFs over a range of Bjorken-$x$ for which both approaches are reliable. Experimental determinations of transversity PDFs carry uncertainties of 50--100%, while current lattice calculations have achieved comparable or better precision, creating an opportunity for lattice inputs to significantly constrain a global analysis. We evaluate the constraining power of existing lattice QCD computations of transversity window moments and Gaussian windows against current phenomenological PDF. We additionally examine prospective tensor charges in the transversity channel and estimate the PDF uncertainty reduction achievable at current and near-future lattice precision. Our results provide quantitative guidance on which window observables will most constrain global PDF analyses.

hep-ph.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
hep-ph.author: Martin Rosenlyst, Vinh Tran, Oliver Zier, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Thejs Brinckmann, Mads T. Frandsen, Jesús Zavala, Frederik Holt Dihver Christensen, Mikkel Theiss Kristensen
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), connecting microscopic dark-sector physics to nonlinear structure formation. We systematize particle-physics ingredients of representative SIDM models and map microscopic parameters and interactions onto structure-formation simulation inputs. These include internal-state populations and reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, inelastic and dissipative energy exchange, decay rates and recoil kinematics, and modifications to cosmological initial conditions. The numerical framework builds on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work for the moving-mesh code AREPO-2, providing substantial performance gains over AREPO-1. We implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, complemented by a dedicated dark-matter decay module. For strongly forward-peaked interactions, the anisotropic hybrid SIDM scheme combines frequent small-angle drag-diffusion with explicit rare large-angle scattering, achieving speed-ups of up to $\sim100\times$ relative to fully anisotropic Monte Carlo in the tested configurations. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish consistency between equivalent numerical treatments, and reproduce published inelastic and dissipative SIDM benchmarks. The resulting modular framework connects dark-sector models to nonlinear astrophysical predictions, enabling exploration of microscopic interactions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

hep-ph.title: Indirect Dark Matter Detection in the Multi-Messenger Era: Experiments, Systematics, Anomalies, and Prospects for Discovery
hep-ph.author: Muad Ghaith, Khaled Obaideen
hep-ph.abstract: Indirect searches for dark matter (DM) span gamma rays, charged cosmic rays, neutrinos, X-rays, radio emission, the cosmic microwave background (CMB), and the 21~cm signal, but reported constraints and anomalies vary in evidential strength. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature from January 2000 through October 2026 using a structured search strategy.We assess observations through a framework linking particle interactions and halo source terms to propagation or cosmological energy deposition, instrumental response, background modeling, and statistical inference. Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf spheroidal galaxies provide robust GeV-scale benchmarks for DM annihilation, whereas Galactic-center searches offer higher expected signals but depend more on foregrounds and halo profiles. Charged-cosmic-ray measurements are precise but limited by propagation and source uncertainties, while neutrino searches offer complementary sensitivity through solar capture, directional and flavor information, and high-mass annihilation or decay. Several widely discussed signals, including the 3.5~keV line, 511~keV emission, the Galactic-center GeV excess, charged-particle features, cluster radio excesses, and candidate gamma-ray lines remain inconclusive because of limited independent confirmation, uncertain target scaling, spectral degeneracies, or background-modeling limitations.Cosmological observations provide complementary constraints from CMB energy-injection limits and 21~cm measurements of the intergalactic medium. Artificial intelligence increasingly supports reconstruction and inference but requires rigorous calibration and domain-shift validation. The strongest case for DM discovery would require statistically consistent evidence across independent targets, instruments, or messengers, under common particle-physics parameters, and with well-characterized uncertainties.

hep-ph.title: MeV dark matter decay forecasts for the COSI mission
hep-ph.author: Robin Anthony-Petersen, Orion Ning, Yu Watanabe, Benjamin R. Safdi, Maíra Dutra, Francesca Calore, Savitri Gallego, William Guan, Christopher M. Karwin, Alexander Kusenko, Israel Martinez-Castellanos, Shigeki Matsumoto, Michela Negro, Uwe Oberlack, Field R. Rogers, Thomas Siegert, Tadayuki Takahashi, Haoyu Xie, Hiroki Yoneda, Andreas Zoglauer, Steven E. Boggs, Dieter H. Hartmann, Carolyn A. Kierans, John A. Tomsick
hep-ph.abstract: The decay of dark matter (DM) is a generic prediction of many particle physics models, producing distinctive monochromatic signatures in environments such as the Galactic halo. Searches for decaying DM in the elusive 'MeV gap' have remained conspicuously under-explored, despite well-motivated models including axion-like particles, sterile neutrinos, and hidden-sector scenarios predicting signatures in this energy range. The upcoming Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) telescope will help bridge this gap. Designed to probe this energy band with high spectral resolution, low background, and wide field of view, COSI is well-suited for DM line searches at the MeV scale. In this work, we make projections for COSI's 2-year sensitivity for DM decay in the Milky Way halo using dedicated all-sky simulations incorporating COSI's predicted instrument response. We conclude that COSI will improve the sensitivity to the DM lifetime by more than an order of magnitude over the DM mass range 0.4 to 10 MeV.

hep-ph.title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
hep-ph.author: Bikram Keshari Pradhan, Jérôme Margueron, Guy Chanfray, Hubert Hansen
hep-ph.abstract: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $\pi+\omega$ and $\pi+\omega+\rho$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $\rho$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

hep-ph.title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
hep-ph.author: Shuochong Han, Xiangdong Sun, Zhenyu Zhu, Ang Li
hep-ph.abstract: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $\beta$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $\beta$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $\Gamma_{\rm th}(\rho_{\rm b},T,\beta)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

hep-ph.title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
hep-ph.author: Yan Huang, Máté Csanád
hep-ph.abstract: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of Lévy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional Lévy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(\rho)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(\rho_{\rm out},\rho_{\rm side},\rho_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic Lévy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

hep-ph.title: Shear viscosity from fluctuations in linearized relativistic hydrodynamics
hep-ph.author: Jakub Sterba, Iurii Karpenko, Marlene Nahrgang, Boris Tomasik
hep-ph.abstract: In this work we incorporate thermal fluctuations into fluid-dynamic simulations with the vHLLE code, in linear approximation. The fluctuations are built in following the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The effect of space discretization into cells in numerical hydrodynamics on the spatial correlation of fluctuations is studied with the help of static structure factor. A difference from the continuum result is pointed out and systematically investigated. Time evolution of the ensuing fluctuations is examined and the Green-Kubo formula is used for the extraction of shear viscosity from the fluctuations. The extracted value is demonstrated to be the same as the input value of the shear viscosity for the simulations using Israel-Stewart equations. It is also shown that numerical regulators commonly used in the codes to ensure stability of the calculation severely spoil the fluctuations and break the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

hep-ph.title: Multimessenger Constraints on Nuclear Acceleration in Neutrino-Emitting Seyfert Coronae
hep-ph.author: Chengchao Yuan
hep-ph.abstract: High-energy neutrinos from Seyfert galaxies probe particle acceleration near supermassive black holes, but the accelerated nuclear composition remains uncertain. We connect stochastic acceleration to nuclear and radiative cascades to assess nuclear contributions. Acceleration and losses limit the energy per nucleon available to nuclear cascades; without secondary reacceleration, fragmentation cannot raise this scale. For NGC~1068, joint neutrino and gamma-ray constraints depend on the nuclear mixture: helium-dominated injection permits larger nuclear power fractions than the heavier mixtures considered. For the harder candidate {neutrino} spectrum of NGC~7469, the adopted model yields more energetic nuclear cascades, while the source-specific flux selections allow larger nuclear fractions for the heavier mixtures than in NGC~1068. These results show that composition constraints depend on nuclear yields as well as acceleration conditions and available power.

hep-ph.title: Probing the proton structure with minimum bias and low-pt dimuon events at hadron colliders
hep-ph.author: Kyle Cormier
hep-ph.abstract: This paper presents two methods for probing the proton structure and the number of partonic interactions in proton-proton collisions using dimuon production and minimum bias events. At the LHC these targeted measurements can provide information on the average number of partonic scatters in different event classes, their dependence on the partonic momentum fraction, x, and potentially partonic flavour. Within a simple mostly geometric model of multiparton interactions as quasi-independent scatters, the measurements can be used to make inference about the proton-proton overlap dependence on impact parameter and its partonic-x dependence.

hep-ph.title: Exact two-loop gravitational tail integrals and their ultraviolet-infrared structure
hep-ph.author: Gabriel Luz Almeida
hep-ph.abstract: Gravitational tail-of-tail corrections arise when radiation scatters twice from the mass-monopole field of its source. In the multipolar effective field theory, one of the two-loop topologies contributing to this process involves genuinely coupled loop momenta, preventing its evaluation through nested one-loop integrations. After tensor reduction, this nonfactorizing structure leads to a particularly challenging family of scalar integrals with unbounded numerator powers as the multipole rank increases. We derive exact closed-form expressions for the entire relevant integer numerator domain, valid in generic dimension and accommodating Feynman, retarded, and advanced prescriptions through consistent analytic continuation. Near $d=3+\epsilon$, we also obtain explicit Laurent expansions through $O(\epsilon)$, retaining the subleading information needed in higher-order radiative calculations. While these expansions determine the dimensional poles, identifying their ultraviolet (UV) or infrared (IR) origin requires a separate analysis of momentum regions. We carry out this analysis throughout the integral domain and apply it directly to the coupled tail-of-tail emission diagram for arbitrary electric and magnetic multipoles. In this way, we independently determine the UV and IR residues, and explicitly verify that the complete infrared pole structure, including both double and simple poles, agrees with the exponentiation of the one-loop gravitational tail. The UV residues, calculated directly from hard-momentum regions, reproduce the established multipole anomalous dimensions when combined with the known contributions of the remaining diagrams.

hep-ph.title: A 4D $T^\prime$-expanded lattice QCD equation of state with a multi-dimensional 3D-Ising-type critical contribution
hep-ph.author: Francesco Di Clemente, Prachi Garella, Johannes Jahan, Micheal Kahangirwe, Jamie M. Karthein, Jacquelyn Noronha-Hostler, Claudia Ratti, Mikhail Stephanov
hep-ph.abstract: Inferring the possible existence and location of a critical point on the QCD phase diagram through experimental observations requires equations of state that include both lattice QCD constraints and critical behavior. In this manuscript, we present the first four-dimensional equation of state in the $(T,\mu_B,\mu_Q,\mu_S)$ space combining the lattice 4D $T^\prime$-Expansion Scheme with a critical contribution mapped from the 3D Ising model. We extend the earlier two-dimensional construction, the so-called Ising 2D-TExS in the $(T, \mu_B)$ plane, promoting the critical point to a parametrizable critical surface in the full four-dimensional thermodynamic space. Our framework provides a family of equations of state to systematically study the effects of criticality in realistic hydrodynamic simulations with $BQS$ conserved charges, going beyond the case of strangeness neutrality, by varying the geometry of the critical surface and the strength of criticality at finite $\mu_B$, $\mu_Q$ and $\mu_S$ separately.

hep-ph.title: A method to challenge symmetries in data with self-supervised learning
hep-ph.author: Rupert Tombs, Christopher G. Lester
hep-ph.abstract: Symmetries are key properties of physical models and of experimental designs, but any proposed symmetry may or may not be realized in nature. In this paper, we introduce a practical and general method to test such suspected symmetries in data, with minimal external input. Self-supervision, which derives learning objectives from data without external labelling, is used to train models to predict 'which is real?' between real data and symmetrically transformed alternatives. If these models make successful predictions in independent tests, then they challenge the targeted symmetries. Crucially, our method handles filtered data, which often arise from inefficiencies or deliberate selections, and which could give the illusion of asymmetry if mistreated. We use examples to demonstrate how the method works and how the models' predictions can be interpreted. Code and data are available atthis https URL.

hep-ph.title: Triggering Higgs vacuum decay
hep-ph.author: Alessandro Strumia
hep-ph.abstract: The Standard Model Higgs potential seems unstable at field values $h > h_{\rm top} \sim 10^{10}$ GeV. Vacuum decay can be triggered by $N\sim 4\pi/\lambda \sim 1000$ overlapped Higgs bosons with energy $\sqrt{\lambda} h_{\rm top}$. However, this configuration is stimulated by ultra-high energy collisions with a $\exp(-{\cal O}(N))$ suppression, comparable to spontaneous vacuum decay: no `Higgspolosion' enhancement arises. This implies that ultra-high energy cosmic ray collisions are safe, despite that their number (in production sites) likely is tens of orders of magnitude higher than what usually estimated (in space). We speculate on how vacuum decay could be induced classically at futuristic ultra-high energy colliders (either using a few right-handed electron beams, or a double collision producing an in-coming wave of $N$ boosted Higgs bosons) and on how the resulting vacuum bubble could be controlled to extract energy.

hep-ph.title: Bayesian Inference of the Critical Endpoint in 2+1-Flavor System from Holographic QCD
hep-ph.author: Liqiang Zhu, Xun Chen, Kai Zhou, Hanzhong Zhang, Mei Huang
hep-ph.abstract: We present a Bayesian holographic model constructed by integrating the equation of state and baryon number susceptibility at zero chemical potential from lattice QCD. The model incorporates error estimates derived from lattice data. With this model, we systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of the 2+1-flavor QCD system. Using Bayesian Inference, we perform precise calibration of the model parameters and determined the critical endpoint (CEP) position under the maximum a posterior (MAP) estimation to be $(T^{c},\mu_{B}^{c})=(0.0859\;\mathrm{GeV},0.742\;\mathrm{GeV})$. Additionally, we predict the CEP positions within 68\% and 95\% confidence levels, yielding $(T^{c},\; \mu_{B}^{c})_{68\%}$=$(0.0820\text{--}0.0889, 0.71\text{--}0.77)\;\mathrm{GeV}$ and $(T^{c},\; \mu_{B}^{c})_{95\%}$=$(0.0816\text{--}0.0898,\; 0.71\text{--}0.79)\;\mathrm{GeV}$, respectively. Moreover, to validate the reliability and predictive power of our approach, we conduct a comprehensive comparison between our predictions and potential CEP locations proposed by other theoretical models. This work not only establishes a novel Bayesian framework for holographic modeling but also provides valuable insights and theoretical support for exploring phase transitions in strongly-interacting matter under extreme conditions.

hep-ph.title: Radiative Transitions for the Ground and Excited Charmonia States
hep-ph.author: Anurag Yadav, Satyajit Puhan, Harleen Dahiya
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we have investigated the physical properties like decay constants, radiative transitions, decay widths, and branching ratios for the ground and radially excited charmonia states. For the numerical calculations, we have adopted the light-front quark model (LFQM). We have studied $\chi_{c0}\rightarrow J/\psi+\gamma $ and $\psi(2S)\rightarrow\chi_{c0}+\gamma$, $h_c(1P)\rightarrow\eta_c(1S)+\gamma $, and $\eta_c(2S)\rightarrow h_c(1P)+\gamma $ transitions in this work. We have also studied the $Q^2$ dependence of the electric dipole transition form factors (TFFs) for all four transitions and compared them with the available lattice QCD and basis light-front quantization (BLFQ) results. Using the TFFs results, we have calculated the decay widths and branching ratios for these transitions. The electric dipole matrix element is decomposed into its Lorentz structures and $E_1(Q^2)$ is extracted from a combination of the longitudinal and transverse plus-current amplitudes canceling the accompanying Coulomb form factor identically. The light-front spin-orbit wave functions of the $P$-wave states $\chi_{c0}$ ($^3P_0$) and $h_c$ ($^1P_1$) are constructed from the Melosh transformation of the corresponding $|(LS)JJ_z\rangle$ states, rather than from the $S$-wave pseudo-scalar and vector ones. The charm quark mass and the harmonic scale are fixed by a variational fit to the two $1S$ masses alone. Our numerical results of decay constants, decay widths, and branching ratios are overall in good agreement with available experimental, theoretical and lattice simulation data.

hep-ph.title: Electron-Ion Collider as a Discovery Tool for Invisible Dark Bosons
hep-ph.author: Hooman Davoudiasl, Hongkai Liu
hep-ph.abstract: We illustrate how the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) can be used to discover dark bosons with masses in the $\sim$ (10~MeV -- 10~GeV) regime, having a wide range of properties. We only require that the dark bosons have a non-negligible weak coupling to electrons and decay with $\ord{1}$ branching fraction into invisible final states. Our signal selection takes advantage of the excellent electron beam kinematic measurements and the capability to tag incoherent scattering, as envisioned at the EIC. This makes the EIC a powerful tool for uncovering potential dark sector forces, for a variety of possibilities.

hep-ph.title: Spectral function approach in NuWro: modeling of multinucleon final states in quasielastic scattering
hep-ph.author: Artur M. Ankowski, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, Jan T. Sobczyk, José L. Bonilla, Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Beata E. Kowal, Hemant Prasad
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrino-oscillation experiments performed in the few-GeV energy region create an urgent demand for a significant improvement in the accuracy of modeling of neutrino interactions with atomic nuclei. Here, we report an updated implementation of the spectral function approach in the \nuwro{} Monte Carlo generator, which consistently treats multinucleon final-states in quasielastic scattering at the inclusive and exclusive level. After validating its accuracy against inclusive electron-scattering data, we compare its predictions to various neutrino cross sections from MicroBooNE. We find that with the multinucleon contribution, these data are reproduced with values of $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom of 0.8--2.5, compared to 2.3--7.3 without it

hep-ph.title: A brief introduction to dispersive methods
hep-ph.author: Gilberto Colangelo
hep-ph.abstract: These lectures aim to provide a basic introduction to dispersive methods and their modern applications to the phenomenology of the Standard Model at low energy. This approach exploits analyticity properties of Green functions and scattering amplitude, often combined with unitarity constraints. To find a logically coherent set of topics in this vast subject, I start with the two-point Green's function, show that this needs the three-point function as input which in turn needs the four-point function. The sequence stops here, just like these lectures, because the four-point function is related only to itself (if one ignores inelastic effects), I will discuss these dispersion relations both in the case of toy models, simple scalar theories, as well as in the phenomenologically relevant case of QCD.

hep-ph.title: Effective Theory for Light Portal Dark Matter Detection
hep-ph.author: Qing Chen, Shuang-Yong Zhou
hep-ph.abstract: We develop a general framework for the computation of light portal dark matter direct detection, incorporating a consistent treatment of finite momentum transfer. In this framework, dark matter interacts with Standard Model matter through a light mediator, which simultaneously serves as the force carrier for dark matter self-interaction, potentially with a distinct coupling strength. The corresponding effective theory relevant for detecting this class of dark matter is systematically constructed. Our analysis focuses on light (semi)relativistic dark matter, which may originate from cosmic-ray boosting and can be probed in high threshold experiments such as large-volume neutrino detectors. In this context, the nucleon matrix elements of the effective operators at finite momentum transfer are required, made available through recent advances in lattice QCD and related nonperturbative methods. The relativistic Fermi gas model is used to convert the nucleon-level momentum transfer to the nuclear level, thereby incorporating nuclear effects pertinent to heavy target experiments. To demonstrate the utility of the framework, we present ultraviolet-complete examples featuring spin-1 and spin-2 portal dark matter. For these models, we compute the differential cross sections with respect to momentum transfer, adopting parameter choices that address the so-called core-cusp problem in astrophysical observations via dark matter self-interactions.

hep-ph.title: Perturbative aspects of the electroweak phase transition with a complex singlet and implications for gravitational wave predictions
hep-ph.author: Thomas Biekötter, Andrii Dashko, Maximilian Löschner, Georg Weiglein
hep-ph.abstract: We present a detailed analysis of strong first-order electroweak phase transitions within the extension of the Standard Model by a complex scalar singlet (cxSM). Focusing on the impact of renormalization scale and gauge dependence, we systematically compare commonly used perturbative frameworks for predicting thermodynamic observables that characterize the phase transition and the associated gravitational-wave (GW) spectrum. These include both the four-dimensional ($4D$) formalism and the dimensionally reduced three-dimensional effective field theory ($3D$ EFT) approach in different renormalization schemes. Within the $3D$ EFT, we compute the effective potential up to two-loop order in a general $R_\xi$ gauge, and demonstrate that applying the $\hbar$-expansion yields gauge-independent results in excellent agreement with those obtained from a direct minimization of the loop-corrected potential. In contrast, large discrepancies between the two methods persist in the $4D$ approaches. We find that, across most of the parameter space, the $3D$ EFT approach provides predictions for phase-transition parameters and GW spectra with theoretical uncertainties in the GW peak amplitude that are reduced by more than an order of magnitude compared to the $4D$ calculations.
