hep-ph.abstract: We study the effects of dimension-four and dimension-six nonminimal Higgs couplings to the Ricci scalar $R$ in the $R^2$-Higgs inflation model in light of the recent ACT and SPT observations. We show that the dimension-six operators $|\Phi|^2 R^2$ and $|\Phi|^4 R$ can accommodate the enhanced scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by the combined CMB+BAO analyses. Using a doubly covariant formalism, we find that the same region of parameter space that explains the observed value of $n_s$ can also induce rapid preheating through the production of the Goldstone modes. If thermalization proceeds efficiently through this preheating mechanism, it may help match the inflationary scale with the CMB reference scale.

hep-ph.title: Can a slow and strong phase transition in neutron stars relieve major compact-star observation tensions?
hep-ph.author: Chen Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: Recent anomalous compact-star observations challenge the conventional neutron-star interpretation in complementary ways: HESS J1731--347 and XTE J1814--338 favor unusually small radii at low mass, while the secondary component of GW190814 appears too massive for an ordinary neutron star under GW170817-based maximum-mass inferences. We examine whether neutron stars with a strong first-order hadron-quark phase transition can address these tensions via the extended stable hybrid branches that arise when the phase conversion is slow compared to radial oscillations, while remaining consistent with GW170817 and NICER constraints. Using a piecewise-polytropic (PP) benchmark, supplemented by an independent speed-of-sound (CS) parametrization comparison, we find two viable scenarios after a general parameter scan over both the hadronic and hybrid branches. Scenario 1 realizes an all-at-once solution: the same equation of state has a pure hadronic branch compatible with both the GW190814-scale mass and HESS J1731--347, while its slow stable hybrid branch reaches XTE J1814--338. Scenario 2 retains the GW190814-scale hadronic branch but reaches XTE J1814--338 and HESS J1731--347 on slow stable hybrid branches in very different transition-strength regimes.

hep-ph.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in the Schwinger Model under a Strong External Electric Field
hep-ph.author: Haobin Chen, Lin Cheng, Xingyu Guo
hep-ph.abstract: We use the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a finite lattice system under a constant external electric field. The lattice Hamiltonian is constructed under open boundary conditions. The vacuum state is prepared using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Scans over the external field strength show the flip of the vacuum state at several field strengths. The critical field strengths agree with theoretical predictions. We further investigate the real-time evolution of the zero-field vacuum under an external electric field using a second-order Trotter-Suzuki decomposition. By comparison with exact diagonalization (ED), we verify that the quantum-simulation protocol reproduces the main features of field-induced boundary charge separation, decay of the vacuum-state fidelity, and quasiperiodic energy redistribution between the electric-field energy term and the fermionic sector. Our results indicate that combining VQE-based state preparation with digital real-time evolution provides a useful approach for studying nonequilibrium dynamics in strong-field lattice gauge theories.

hep-ph.title: Decoupling Limit of Quiver Theories and the Angular Spectra of Extreme C-metrics
hep-ph.author: Peng Yang, Kilar Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the angular eigenvalue problem of the extreme charged C-metric. Starting from a constrained five-point Fuchsian description of the non-extremal angular equation, we obtain its extreme limit by decoupling a hypermultiplet in the dual four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$, $\mathrm{SU(2)}\times \mathrm{SU(2)}$ linear quiver gauge theory. We derive the parameter dictionary and renormalized Matone relations, and connect the physical limit $Q\to M$ to the quiver decoupling by an explicit coordinate transformation. Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.

hep-ph.title: Cosmological Vacuum Decays from Schwinger-Keldysh Formalism
hep-ph.author: Zi-Yan Yuwen
hep-ph.abstract: In this work, we take a first step to a stochastic real-time description of the vacuum phase transitions in a radiation-dominated FLRW universe from the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. By splitting the phase transition field $\Phi$ into the long-wavelength mode $\phi$ and the short-wavelength mode $\sigma$ and tracing over the latter as the environment, we obtain a classical Langevin-type equation-of-motion for the long-wavelength field $\phi$, where the quantum effects are encoded in a non-Markov memory kernel and a non-Gaussian noise. As a phenomenological example, we start from a polynomial potential and a thermalized initial state, and study the structure of the memory kernel as well as the correlation functions of the noise term. Further extensions remain possible to describe the whole dynamics of cosmological first-order phase transitions via numerical simulations.

hep-ph.title: Confining density functional approach to the QCD phase diagram at low temperatures and thermal twin stars
hep-ph.author: David Blaschke, Oleksii Ivanytskyi
hep-ph.abstract: We present a density functional-based equation of state for warm, dense nuclear matter with a transition to deconfined quark matter for applications to simulations of supernova explosions and neutron star mergers, but also for the cosmological evolution of Q-balls. For the quark matter equation of state, we employ a recently developed confining density functional approach while nuclear matter is described within a relativistic density functional model of the DD2 class. The phase transition is obtained by a Maxwell construction at constant entropy per baryon. We discuss the solutions of TOV equations for isentropic hybrid stars for two hybrid equation of state models: DDf-SFM without and DD2-$\chi$CDF with color superconductivity. We find that at finite temperatures above a critical value of entropy per baryon sequences of disconnected third family branches ("thermal twin stars") may appear for the DDf-SFM model, while they are absent for the color superconducting model and at $T=0$. We discuss the relation of this critical entropy per baryon to the Seidov criterion of gravitational instability for $T=0$ and find that it is a good guide. We suggest that the presence of thermal twin stars may be regarded as an indicator for the core-collapse supernova explodability of massive blue supergiant stars with solar metallicity and thus serve as a new criterion for the reliability of hybrid equation of state models. By this argument, strong color superconductivity shall be excluded and it remains to be shown whether models with moderate diquark pairing could fulfill the thermal twin constraint. For the case of symmetric matter, we compare the resulting hybrid EOS with the flow constraint by Danielewicz et al. and find a a sensitivity of the onset density for deconfinement to the presence or absence of color superconductivity.

hep-ph.title: Non-perturbative news from the conformal window
hep-ph.author: Álvaro Pastor-Gutiérrez
hep-ph.abstract: Dynamical symmetry breaking plays a crucial role in mass and scale generation. In QCD-like theories, its dependence on the number of fermion flavours determines the phase structure and the transition to the conformal regime. In this work, we compute non-perturbative corrections relevant to this phenomenom, including momentum dependencies and field invariants essential for an adequate realisation of the global symmetries, by means of the functional renormalisation group and the generalised flow equation. We find that the critical gauge coupling required for dynamical chiral symmetry breaking acquires a strong dependence on the number of flavours and increases sharply at $N_f^\textrm{crit}\simeq 7.30$ for $N_c=3$. This establishes a new picture of the phase transition to the conformal window that disfavours Miransky/BKT scaling and walking regimes but supports a first-order quantum phase transition and a critical region with exotic dynamics and symmetric fermion mass gaps.

hep-ph.title: Symmetry-Restoring Counter-terms in Massive Gauge Theories with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ via Gauge-Invariant Sector Decomposition
hep-ph.author: Andrea Quadri
hep-ph.abstract: We compute the one-loop breaking of the Slavnov-Taylor (ST) identities in a massive Abelian chiral gauge theory with spontaneous symmetry breaking, regularized in the Breitenlohner-Maison-`t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. We also provide the one-loop finite counter-terms required to restore the one-loop ST identities. The recent formulation of spontaneously broken models based on the Fröhlich-Morchio-Strocchi (FMS) gauge-invariant and dynamical (i.e. propagating inside loops) fields is used. The proposed algebraic approach holds true to all orders in the loop expansion and allows for a consistent decomposition of the ST breaking into independent sectors. By using cohomological techniques we eventually constrain the dependence of the ST breaking on the vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field. This yields a set of differential equations that provide a useful check of the mass-dependent terms in the ST breaking terms in the broken phase. They can be generalized to the non-Abelian case, both in the gauge-invariant formalism and in the conventional one. In the massless limit we find agreement with previous calculations present in the literature.

hep-ph.title: Scalar Perturbations and Induced Gravitational Waves from First-Order Phase Transitions in Lattice Simulations
hep-ph.author: Yuan-Jie Li, Jing Liu, Zhuan Ning, Xiang-Xi Zeng, Zong-Kuan Guo
hep-ph.abstract: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can generate curvature perturbations through inhomogeneous quantum tunneling, as studied previously on superhorizon scales. In this work, we for the first time conduct three-dimensional lattice simulations that incorporate scalar metric perturbations and radiation perturbations, covering a range from bubble wall scales to super-horizon scales. We obtain the precise scalar perturbation power spectrum and the probability density function of energy density perturbations. Furthermore, we simulate the gravitational-wave energy spectra generated by each source during the first-order phase transition, including the scalar field itself, scalar metric perturbations, and the energy density and velocity perturbations of radiation. For gravitational waves, the contribution from other sources can exceed $1/3$ of that from the scalar field at superhorizon scales. Additionally, we compare the effects of different values of the transition strength and rate on the results. This paper provides more accurate numerical results for research aimed at detecting or constraining first-order phase transitions via gravitational waves and curvature perturbations.

hep-lat.title: Perturbative Renormalization of Noether Currents in SYM with Improved Discretizations
hep-lat.author: Marios Costa, Elias Antoniou, Salomi Dimou, Constantinos Costa, Panos K. Chrysanthis, Gregoris Spanoudes, Haralambos Panagopoulos
hep-lat.abstract: We investigate the perturbative renormalization of Noether currents associated with chiral symmetry and supersymmetry transformations in $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, regularized on the lattice using improved discretizations. In particular, we study the chiral current and the supercurrent operator for a broad class of lattice actions: Wilson fermions with one-step stout-smeared links and a clover term, together with a family of Symanzik-improved gluon actions. Since the supercurrent mixes with both gauge-invariant and gauge-noninvariant operators, we compute the corresponding renormalization factors and mixing coefficients at one-loop order. We analyze the impact of improved gluon and gluino actions on this mixing pattern and investigate whether suitable choices of lattice parameters, such as the clover and stout coefficients, can reduce unwanted lattice artifacts at one loop. Our results provide perturbative input for the implementation of Ward identities and for matching lattice observables to their continuum counterparts, while also offering guidance for simulations aimed at restoring supersymmetry in the continuum limit.

hep-lat.title: Impact of Window Observables on the Transversity Quark Parton Distribution Function
hep-lat.author: Daniel Adamiak, Christopher Monahan
hep-lat.abstract: We study the potential impact of lattice QCD window observables on nucleon isovector quark transversity parton distribution functions (PDFs) using the ePump Hessian-updating framework. Window observables, recently proposed inarXiv:2505.22795as benchmark quantities enabling direct quantitative comparison between lattice QCD and phenomenological PDF extractions, are weighted integrals of PDFs over a range of Bjorken-$x$ for which both approaches are reliable. Experimental determinations of transversity PDFs carry uncertainties of 50--100%, while current lattice calculations have achieved comparable or better precision, creating an opportunity for lattice inputs to significantly constrain a global analysis. We evaluate the constraining power of existing lattice QCD computations of transversity window moments and Gaussian windows against current phenomenological PDF. We additionally examine prospective tensor charges in the transversity channel and estimate the PDF uncertainty reduction achievable at current and near-future lattice precision. Our results provide quantitative guidance on which window observables will most constrain global PDF analyses.

hep-lat.title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
hep-lat.author: Praveen Balaji, Patrick Draper, Enrico Rinaldi
hep-lat.abstract: Quantum computing may allow unprecedented access to nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, including problems of interest in particle physics, like the real-time development of scattering processes. Although fault-tolerant simulations at scale are still in the future, recent advancements toward early fault-tolerant simulations motivate building increasingly elaborate benchmark problems in order to assess state-of-the-art capabilities and test new algorithms and observables. In this work, we study glueball scattering on a line-of-plaquettes lattice in pure $SU(3)$ lattice gauge theory. We characterize scattering of the lowest-energy glueball states using classical exact diagonalization methods, identifying the continuum resonance structure using real-time simulations and approximate analytic methods, and we propose time-domain observables for extracting properties of the resonance from quantum simulations. We furthermore construct a toy model that shares the spectral features of the lattice gauge theory and demonstrate extraction of the observables. Feasibility on near-term hardware is demonstrated through simulation of a resonant collision of this toy model on Quantinuum System Model $\texttt{H2-2}$, with a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits. The Trotterized circuit after optimization and compression requires $\sim 25n$ entangling gates for $n$ Trotter steps.

hep-lat.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
hep-lat.author: Dennis Grinwald, Ankur Singha, Khaled Kahouli, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima
hep-lat.abstract: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Diffusion models are promising for this purpose, but their standard denoising score matching objective requires samples from the target distribution, seemingly reintroducing the original sampling problem. Here, we show that diffusion models can instead be trained from their own generated samples using the target score identity, provided access to the unnormalized probability density. Importance-weighted formulations of this identity yield a consistent target throughout training, while unweighted variants define a self-consistent fixed-point training scheme. We benchmark the different approaches in two-dimensional \(\phi^4\) theory and identify effective choices that enable efficient training and sampling across the symmetric, critical, and broken phases. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.

hep-lat.title: Solutions of Roy equations for variable pion mass
hep-lat.author: Gilberto Colangelo
hep-lat.abstract: The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pionmasses below the physical value in the region between threshold and$s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that thephenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentiallyunchanged. Moreover, for $M_\pi \le M_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiralperturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengthsprovide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. Theoutcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves asthe light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test ofthe approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$,$P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreementwith chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_\pi \leM_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion massesabove the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resultingsolutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_\pi=239\MeV$. Thepresent work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fullyincorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossingsymmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependenceof the $\sigma$ and $\rho$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both ofwhich will be addressed in future work.

hep-lat.title: Signal-to-noise problems in fault-tolerant quantum computation
hep-lat.author: Hyunwoo Oh
hep-lat.abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising alternative to classical Monte Carlo methods by naturally avoiding sign problems through unitary evolution. A common misconception follows from this: because quantum simulation sidesteps the sign problem, it is often assumed to be an essentially perfect substitute for classical sampling. This is false---quantum measurements are intrinsically stochastic, and estimating observables often requires a number of samples that grows exponentially with system size, time separation, or inverse temperature, exactly as in the classical signal-to-noise problem. In this work, we analyze the origin and structure of signal-to-noise problems in quantum computation, drawing parallels with classical Monte Carlo, and demonstrate that such noise persists even in sign-problem-free regimes. We discuss strategies to mitigate it, in particular a quantum generalization of Stein control variates construction, in which unbiased estimators are built from operator commutators $[X,A]$ and their discrete diagonal counterparts, and validate the approach with exactly solvable numerical examples that quantify the achievable variance reduction. Our results underscore that variance reduction, not merely sign-problem avoidance, is required to make quantum algorithms practically viable for many-body physics.

hep-lat.title: Lepton Flavour Universality in Semileptonic $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$ Transitions
hep-lat.author: Yu-Chen Hu, Cong-Cong Ye, Craig D. Roberts, Zhao-Qian Yao
hep-lat.abstract: Using continuum Schwinger function methods, we deliver parameter-free pointwise predictions for the complete set of twelve Standard Model (SM) $\bar B_{(s)} \to D_{(s)}^{(\ast)}$, i.e., $b\to c$, semileptonic transition form factors on the entire kinematically accessible domain. Therewith, we calculate SM theory values for the decay-rate ratios of $\tau$ and $\mu$ final states: $\{ R(D) \, , \, R(D)^\ast \} = \{ 0.290(11) \, , \, 0.267(5) \}$, $\{ R(D_{s}) \, , \, R(D_{s}^{\ast}) \} = \{ 0.283(11) \, , \, 0.251(5) \}$. The former is consistent with an existing average of SM estimates, but disagrees with the experimental average by $2.8\sigma$. Comparing transitions with light quark and strange quark spectators, we find a $2.3\sigma$ signal for violation of SU$(3)$ flavour symmetry, expressed at the 5% level in $D_{(s)}^\ast$ final states. It is induced by Higgs boson couplings into the strong interaction and modulated by phenomena deriving from emergent features of the strong interaction.

hep-lat.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
hep-lat.author: Ali Rayat, Gia-Wei Chern
hep-lat.abstract: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.

hep-lat.title: On Ising model in magnetic field on the lattice
hep-lat.author: Raghav G. Jha
hep-lat.abstract: We study the free energy of the classical square-lattice Ising model in a uniform real magnetic field $h$, for which no exact solution is known. We first conjecture a closed-form expression built from the one-dimensional Ising chain and Onsager's hypergeometric solution. Comparing with high-precision tensor renormalization group (TRG) data, we find that it deviates by up to $2.6\%$, has no spontaneous magnetization, and gives an effective critical-isotherm exponent $\delta \to 1$. However, using the Lee--Yang circle theorem, we show that the exact free energy is a superposition of one-dimensional Ising chains in the same field, weighted by a temperature-dependent (normalized, but not always positive) distribution of squared Lee--Yang gaps, of which our first expression is a single-chain approximation. Exact results (Onsager, Yang, the strong-field expansion and the Lee--Yang solution at $\beta h = i\pi/2$) become sum rules for this distribution. We propose a simple form for it, fixed by Onsager's free energy and the exact strong-field limit without any fit to numerical data. This \emph{improved} conjecture agrees with TRG to $0.15\%$ for all $\beta$ and $h$, reproduces Yang's spontaneous magnetization exactly, has a positive specific heat, and yields the critical isotherm $M\propto h^{1/\delta}$ with $\delta = 15.2$ and amplitude $1.055$, compared with the exact $\delta=15$ and $1.059$. A refined form, which builds in additional input from Ising field theory (including the exact critical isotherm, $\delta=15$) and a few constants adjusted to transfer-matrix and TRG data, matches the TRG free energy to $4\times 10^{-5}$.

hep-lat.title: The Arf-Brown-Kervaire invariant on a lattice
hep-lat.author: Sho Araki, Hidenori Fukaya, Tetsuya Onogi, Satoshi Yamaguchi
hep-lat.abstract: We propose a lattice formulation of the Arf-Brown-Kervaire (ABK) invariant which takes values in $\mathbb{Z}_8$. Compared to the standard $\mathbb{Z}$-valued index, the ABK invariant is more involved in that it arises in Majorana fermion partition functions with reflection symmetry on two-dimensional non-orientable manifolds, and its definition contains an infinite sum over Dirac eigenvalues that requires proper regularization. We employ the massive Wilson Dirac operator, with and without domain-walls, on standard two-dimensional square lattices, and use its Pfaffian for the definition. Twisted boundary conditions and cross-caps, which reverse the orientation, are introduced to realize nontrivial topologies equipped with nontrivial $\mathrm{Pin}^{-}$ structures of Majorana fermions. We verify numerically (and partly analytically) that our formulation on a torus, Klein bottle, real projective plane (as well as its triple connected sum), and two types of Möbius strip reproduces the known values in continuum theory.

hep-lat.title: Symmetric Mass Generation as a Multicritical Point with Enhanced Symmetry
hep-lat.author: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic
hep-lat.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of a lattice fermion model that exhibits three distinct phases: a massless fermion phase, a massive fermion phase with spontaneous symmetry breaking induced by a fermion bilinear condensate, and a massive fermion phase with symmetric mass generation. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method on large cubical lattices, we find evidence for traditional second-order critical points separating the first two and the latter two phases. Remarkably, these critical points appear to merge at a multicritical point with enhanced symmetry when the symmetry breaking parameter is tuned to zero, giving rise to the recently discovered direct second-order transition between the massless and symmetric massive fermion phases.

hep-lat.title: Phase diagram of a lattice fermion model with symmetric mass generation
hep-lat.author: Sandip Maiti, Debasish Banerjee, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Marina K. Marinkovic
hep-lat.abstract: We study the phase structure of a model containing two flavors of massless staggered fermions interacting through two independent four-fermion couplings, UI and UB, formulated on a three-dimensional Euclidean space-time lattice. At UB = 0, this model is known to exhibit a direct second-order quantum phase transition between a massless fermion (MF) phase and a phase in which fermions acquire masses through the mechanism commonly referred to as symmetric mass generation (SMG). We demonstrate that introducing a small nonzero value of UB qualitatively alters this structure: the single exotic transition at UB = 0 splits into two distinct, conventional transitions, separated by an intermediate phase in which fermion masses arise through the standard mechanism of spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB). The first of these is a Gross-Neveu transition separating the MF phase from the SSB-induced massive phase, while the second is a three-dimensional XY transition between the SSB phase and the SMG phase. Using the fermion-bag Monte Carlo method, we verify that the critical exponents associated with both transitions are consistent with the literature, thereby yielding a quantitative characterization of the resulting phase structure of the model.

hep-lat.title: Digital Quantum Simulation of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in the Schwinger Model under a Strong External Electric Field
hep-lat.author: Haobin Chen, Lin Cheng, Xingyu Guo
hep-lat.abstract: We use the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model to investigate the nonequilibrium dynamics of a finite lattice system under a constant external electric field. By comparison with exact diagonalization (ED), we verify that the quantum-simulation protocol reproduces the main features of field-induced boundary charge separation, decay of the vacuum-state fidelity, and quasiperiodic energy redistribution between the electric-field energy term and the fermionic sector. hep-lat.title: A brief introduction to dispersive methods
hep-lat.author: Gilberto Colangelo
hep-lat.abstract: These lectures aim to provide a basic introduction to dispersive methods and their modern applications to the phenomenology of the Standard Model at low energy. This approach exploits analyticity properties of Green functions and scattering amplitude, often combined with unitarity constraints. To find a logically coherent set of topics in this vast subject, I start with the two-point Green's function, show that this needs the three-point function as input which in turn needs the four-point function. The sequence stops here, just like these lectures, because the four-point function is related only to itself (if one ignores inelastic effects), I will discuss these dispersion relations both in the case of toy models, simple scalar theories, as well as in the phenomenologically relevant case of QCD.

hep-lat.title: Entanglement in the $θ$-vacuum
hep-lat.author: Sebastian Grieninger, Dmitri E. Kharzeev, Eliana Marroquin
hep-lat.abstract: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $\theta$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $\theta=\pi$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $\theta=\pi$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $\theta=\pi$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.

hep-lat.title: Extraction of charmonium branching fractions from $J/ψ\toγη_c$ radiative decays
hep-lat.author: Magnus C. Schaaf, Antonio Vairo
hep-lat.abstract: We assess the tension between theoretical predictions and the values quoted by the Particle Data Group (PDG) for the partial decay width and branching fraction associated with the radiative charmonium decay $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c$. A profile scan over the most recent PDG data depending on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ suggests that the correlation between measured branching fractions is compatible with lattice QCD determinations of the partial decay widths $\Gamma(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ and $\Gamma(\eta_c\to\gamma\gamma)$. We propose a theoretically grounded photon line shape for the radiative decay spectrum and a prescription for the extraction of (product) branching fractions involving the magnetic dipole (M1) transition $J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c$. This approach obviates the need to modify the photon energy spectrum line shape using empirical damping functions, as done in the most recent experimental extractions of $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi\to\gamma\eta_c)$ from the photon line shape, thereby eliminating an inherent ambiguity in the determination of the derived observables.

hep-lat.title: Neural Non-Equilibrium Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for Corrected Boltzmann Sampling
hep-lat.author: Moxian Qian
hep-lat.abstract: Learned dynamical proposals can generate configurations without providing a tractable endpoint density. Nonequilibrium path probabilities offer a way to correct such proposals, but correction alone does not determine their ability to connect separated regions. We introduce Neural Non-Equilibrium Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (NHMC), which combines conditional momentum distributions with reversible, volume preserving dynamics. The forward--reverse path ratio gives the work used for training, importance weighting, normalizer estimation, and Metropolis correction. We then construct a configuration space round-trip kernel whose reverse and forward paths share an intermediate configuration. Conditional on that configuration, its path record update is independence Metropolis--Hastings. We compare its stationary inter-region flow with the flow obtained under exact conditional matching and bound their difference by the conditional path mismatch. This separates errors in the conditional proposal from dependence between the endpoint region and the intermediate configuration. Many well calculations test normalizers and mode probabilities; a controlled lattice $\phi^4$ calculation compares ideal and accepted inter-sector flows and measures sector relaxation. In two dimensional $U(1)$, $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ gauge theories, corrected path weight estimates reproduce finite volume Wilson loops; $U(1)$ topological susceptibilities are also compared with analytic predictions across several lattice volumes.

hep-lat.title: Prospects for $K_{L}\toπ^{0}ν\barν$, $K_S\toμ^+μ^-$, $K_L\toπ^0 \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\varepsilon^{\prime}/\varepsilon$ after the new $K^{+}\toπ^{+}ν\barν$ result from NA62
hep-lat.author: Monika Blanke, Andrzej J. Buras, Cristina Lazzeroni, Joel C. Swallow

hep-lat.title: Non-perturbative news from the conformal window
hep-lat.author: Álvaro Pastor-Gutiérrez

In QCD-like theories, its dependence on the number of fermion flavours determines the phase structure and the transition to the conformal regime. hep-lat.title: Neutral Pseudoscalar Mesons, Hadron Light-by-Light Scattering, and the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment
hep-lat.author: Cong-Cong Ye, Yu-Chen Hu, Minghui Ding, Craig D. Roberts
hep-lat.abstract: Continuum Schwinger function methods\linebreak (CSM) are used to provide estimates of pseudoscalar meson pole contributions - $\mathsf P = \pi^0$, $\eta$, $\eta^\prime$, $\eta_c$, $\eta_b$ - to the muon anomalous magnetic moment. The analysis framework is benchmarked via successful applications to an array of other meson and nucleon properties. It uses the leading order CSM truncation, augmented by a parametrisation of non-Abelian anomaly effects, to deliver an internally consistent treatment of all the pseudoscalar--two-photon transition form factors required to complete such a calculation. Employing those form factor predictions, the following results are obtained (units $10^{-11}$): $a_\mu^{\pi^0} + a_\mu^{\eta} + a_\mu^{\eta^\prime} = 84.3(0.8)$ - a value lower than some other contemporary estimates; $a_\mu^{\eta_c} = 0.82(0.04)$; and a value of $a_\mu^{\eta_b}$ that is negligible. The total contribution is $\sum _{\mathsf P} a_\mu^{\mathsf P} = 85.1(0.8) / 10^{11}$. Our analysis suggests that this pole contribution to $a_\mu$ is still not known with precision better than 5\%.

hep-th.title: Semiclassical state on algebra of observables for de Sitter space and time reversal symmetry
hep-th.author: Muxin Han, Yichen Hu
hep-th.abstract: In de Sitter static patch holography, coupling bulk quantum fields to an observer's dynamical clock yields a type II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}_+$ of gauge-invariant observables. However, the unique tracial state on this algebra fails to reproduce semiclassical bulk correlation functions. We resolve this issue by introducing a family of heavy-clock states, representing an observer reference frame with heavy inertia. We prove that in the heavy-clock limit, $n$-point correlation functions of gauge-invariant dressed observables reproduce the bulk quantum field correlation functions on de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, we investigate a generalized observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ that incorporates both forward-running ($\pi\geq 0$) and backward-running ($\pi <0$) clocks. The resulting von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ of gauge-invariant observables remains a type~II$_1$ factor and is isomorphic to $\mathcal{M}_+\otimes M_2(\mathbb{C})$, where $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ is the algebra of $2\times2$ complex matrices transforming between the two clock orientations. Time-reversal symmetry is implemented in this setting as an anti-unitary operator that exchanges the two clock orientations, yielding a type~II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{F}$ of gauge-invariant, time-reversal-invariant observables. We generalize the heavy-clock state construction to both $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{F}$, showing that $n$-point correlation functions calculated in heavy-clock states match the corresponding semiclassical bulk correlation functions. Finally, by coupling Einstein gravity to the Brown--Kuchař dust field, we derive the observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ from a perturbative reduction along the observer's worldline in the $G \to 0$ limit. This provides a field-theoretic foundation for the observer model developed in this work.

hep-th.title: Defect conformal field theories with free-in-the-bulk fermions
hep-th.author: Christopher P. Herzog, Daniel Lloyd-Jones
hep-th.abstract: We study codimension-two conformal defects for massless fermions that are free in a four-dimensional bulk, but interact on a two-dimensional defect. The bulk Dirac equation strongly constrains defect conformal field theory data: it fixes the dimensions of operators in the bulk-defect operator product expansion and, for bulk-defect-defect three-point functions, enforces a double-twist relation when only one member of a shadow pair is allowed by unitarity. The lowest modes of monodromy defects provide an important exception, since both shadow partners can be unitary and their three-point functions are instead related by a shadow transform.We illustrate these structures with defect interactions, including an exactly tractable bilinear flow and Gross-Neveu-type quartic couplings. At a perturbative mixed fixed point, we find an explicit interacting example in which the double-twist condition is violated and the two shadow channels combine to give a regular bulk-defect-defect correlation function.

hep-th.title: The dimensional reduction of the spin-3 and spin-4 partially broken Fronsdal models
hep-th.author: D. Dalmazi, A. L. R. dos Santos
hep-th.abstract: Here we perform a Kaluza-Klein dimensional reduction from $D+1$ to $D$ dimensions of a partially broken Fronsdal model for spin-3 and spin-4. The reduced models describe massive spin-3 and spin-4 particles without extra propagating modes. They differ from Singh-Hagen models by quadratic terms which vanish on shell, similarly to their higher dimensional massless parents. A covariant description of the reduced models in terms of gauge invariant field combinations naturally leads to higher derivative models, contrary to lower spin cases ($s\le 2$).For both $s=3$ and $s=4$ we have a rather peculiar massless limit. Although their particle content corresponds to the $\pm j$ helicities with $j=0,1, \cdots s$, as expected, they appear intertwined in a non trivial way preventing diagonalization through any local field redefinition.

hep-th.title: Three-dimensional vacua of $G_2$ flux compactifications
hep-th.author: Aravind Aikot, Julian Choi, Timm Wrase
hep-th.abstract: We study supersymmetric vacua of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ effective theories from type IIA, type IIB/type I, and heterotic compactifications on $G_2$-structure spaces. Superpotential homogeneity and the physical scalar metric yield universal vacuum relations and axion stabilization constraints without specifying the full moduli-space metric. We express AdS$_3$ scalar masses through $\Delta$, the scaling dimension of the corresponding operator in the dual two-dimensional conformal field theory. In massive type IIA AdS$_3$ vacua, we derive the bound $\Delta_{\max}\geq(20+4\sqrt{67})/7\approx 7.5$ and an exact dimension $\Delta_b=6$ for $B_2$ axions on the torsion-free branch. Type IIB type I and heterotic AdS$_3$ vacua contain a universal volume-dilaton mode with $\Delta_{\phi s}=4$. On the singlet-torsion type IIB branch, we also obtain the volume-dilaton mode with $\Delta_{\phi s}=20/7$ and $\Delta_b=16/7$. Every supersymmetric Minkowski vacuum in the retained classical closed-string theories possesses an exact volume-dilaton flat direction. We characterize physical large-flux limits after tadpole constraints and axionic identifications, and identify torsion obstructions to isotropic scale separation.

hep-th.title: One-loop QED effective action at finite temperature and density beyond HTL limit
hep-th.author: Farahmand Hasanov, Nikita Kolganov
hep-th.abstract: We develop a framework for computing the nonlocal one-loop effective action in scalar and spinor QED at finite temperature and chemical potential in arbitrary even spacetime dimensions. Based on the heat kernel expansion to quadratic order in background fields, the framework reduces the effective action form factors to a common fundamental kernel. By resumming the external-momentum expansion, we obtain explicit closed-form expressions for the massless form factors in terms of polylogarithms and their derivatives with respect to the order. The same method determines the coefficients of the small-mass expansion to arbitrary order. The resulting expressions retain the full dependence on external Euclidean momentum, temperature, and chemical potential, without invoking the soft-momentum approximation. We also derive the corresponding photon polarization operators and evaluate their static limits, obtaining the Debye screening masses and electromagnetic susceptibilities.

hep-th.title: Characteristic Modes of Non-minimally Coupled Thick Branes
hep-th.author: Jing-Xin Gong, Heng Guo, Yong-Tao Lu, Xin-Yi Pan
hep-th.abstract: Characteristic modes provide important information about the intrinsic properties and dynamical response of gravitational systems. In this work, we investigate characteristic modes of thick branes with a non-minimally coupled bulk scalar field. Two representative thick brane solutions are considered, corresponding to a single-kink scalar configuration and a deformed kink configuration with internal structure, respectively. By analyzing the tensor perturbation equations, we first examine the localization of the graviton zero mode in the two brane models. For both brane models, the graviton zero mode is localized on the brane. No pronounced resonant Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes are found for the single-kink brane at $\xi=1/7$. For the deformed brane, we investigate the resonant KK modes at $\xi=0.99$, finding that increasing the deformation parameter $k$ leads to more resonant modes and a longer-lived first resonance.We then calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of both brane models independently in the frequency and time domains. The quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) obtained by the independent methods agree well for the low overtones. The masses and decay rates of the resonant KK modes agree closely with the real parts and the magnitudes of the imaginary parts of the corresponding QNFs, respectively.

hep-th.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight
hep-th.author: Tzu-Chen Huang
hep-th.abstract: We construct a chiral algebra $U$ of central charge eight inside the lattice vertex operator algebra $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$. It is generated by two commuting affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ current algebras at levels $1$ and $39$, the stress tensor of the lattice theory, and a single weight-two field built from three lattice exponentials. We announce that $U$ is strongly rational and completely unitary, and that $Rep(U)$ is equivalent, as a unitary ribbon category, to the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category $\mathcal{H}_3$. Its characters are the $\gamma=0$ Evans--Gannon vector. From $U$ we obtain a diagonal full CFT, and also a holomorphic $E_8$ extension on which $\mathcal{H}_3$ acts by topological defects.

hep-th.title: PINNs for N=2* holography
hep-th.author: Alex Buchel
hep-th.abstract: Can a holographic theory be reconstructed from its equation of state? We investigate this question using physics-informed neural networks in the bosonic-mass sector of the Pilch--Warner model. We first validate the PINN approach against an analytic solution encoding the leading high-temperature corrections to the conformal equation of state. We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity. Independent solutions of the bulk Einstein-scalar equations demonstrate that accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential. High-precision knowledge of the high-temperature equation of state constrains nonlinear interactions in the bulk scalar potential. Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value, motivated by this high-temperature extraction, reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of $\sim 15$ compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass. Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity of the gauge theory plasma further reduces this error by an additional factor of $\sim 13$, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within $0.09\%$.

hep-th.title: Bondi Four-Momentum Balance in Quantum NSF Classical matching, DKL supermomentum, and quantum energy redistribution
hep-th.author: Carlos Kozameh, Gerardo DEpaola
hep-th.abstract: We derive Bondi four-momentum balance between past and future null infinity in the radiative phase space of the null-surface formulation (NSF). Weyl matching at spatial infinity, together with vanishing endpoint News, gives antipodal continuity of the Bondi mass aspect. Its translation projection is independent of the infrared shear term and transforms as a Lorentz four-vector. Bondi evolution relates the incoming and outgoing News fluxes to the timelike endpoint momenta; in the Dominguez--Kozameh--Ludvigsen radiative sector these momenta vanish and the fluxes are equal. On a common radiative Fock domain, unitary conjugation transports the flux observables. Adopting their classical balance as an additional quantum condition yields exclusive four-momentum conservation. We also calculate the outgoing energy expectation without imposing that condition. For an incoming energy eigenstate, the second-generator commutator vanishes diagonally, leaving a second-order coefficient determined by the cubic generator. Direct canonical contractions isolate the contribution connected to all four external legs. For the equal-energy center-of-mass preparation, axial rotational covariance forces the angularly integrated exchange coefficient to vanish under the finite helicity-projection prescription of Part~I. The connected energy defect therefore vanishes through second order. The full expectation (including spectators) and higher-order balance remain open.

hep-th.title: A critical coupling for the magnetic instability of holographic SU(2) plasmas
hep-th.author: Migael Strydom
hep-th.abstract: We show that gravity can remove the linear magnetic instability of a holographic plasma with an $SU(2)$ global symmetry. In the probe limit, charged vector bosons become tachyonic in their lowest Landau level above a critical field and condense into a vortex lattice. In Einstein-$SU(2)$ Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_5$ we include the backreaction of the field exactly, expanding only in the condensate around the D'Hoker-Kraus magnetic brane. The critical field diverges as the coupling $\alpha = \kappa^2/\hat g^2$ approaches $\alpha_\star = 2/3$, above which the normal phase has no linear charged instability at any field or temperature: we show this at zero temperature and establish it numerically at finite temperature. At zero temperature the field cancels from the mass of the lowest Landau level in the brane's AdS$_3 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ throat, and the instability is a violation of the throat's Breitenlohner-Freedman bound. The onset temperature vanishes at $\alpha_\star$ with an essential singularity of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. For two-derivative Einstein-Yang-Mills duals in $d = 4$, 5 and 6 dimensions the normal phase has a charged instability if and only if $C_J/C_T < 8/(d^2(d+1))$, one tenth in $d = 4$. Above $\alpha_L = 0.372$ the gravitational attraction between vortices makes the uniform lattice unstable and the transition first order, so $B_c$ is only a spinodal; whether a condensed phase survives above $\alpha_\star$ is left open.

hep-th.title: Charged Deformation of a Hairy Black Brane: Perturbative Solution and Thermodynamics
hep-th.author: Sangheon Yun
hep-th.abstract: We study electrically charged black branes in four-dimensional Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory with Maxwell coupling $Z(\phi)=e^{3\phi/\sqrt7}$, whose potential has an AdS$_4$ fixed point only in the infrared. For nonzero hair parameter $\alpha$ the scalar grows logarithmically at large radius and the geometry is not asymptotically AdS, so the holographic dictionary is a working assumption. With the scale-invariant multi-trace boundary condition of the neutral branes, giving conformal thermodynamics, we work to second order in the charge, obtaining the Maxwell field and susceptibility in closed form, plus the thermodynamics, condensate, incoherent conductivity and cumulant ratio $T^2\chi_4/\chi_2=6c(\alpha)<0$ for all $\alpha$ considered. Independent perturbative computations and first-law closed forms agree within $4\times10^{-6}$; nonlinear solutions reproduce second-order results to $1.2\times10^{-5}$ and $c$ to $6\times10^{-4}$. They are locally thermodynamically stable where constructed, and the pressure is analytic in $(\mu_Q/T)^2$ near zero density. No regular extremal horizon exists at finite scalar value, and $\rho/s<\sqrt{21}/(2\pi)$ exactly. The extremal limit is an AdS$_2\times\mathbb R^2$ throat where the scalar grows as $\ln\ln(1/u)$ in the AdS$_2$ radial coordinate $u$; the bound is saturated there, and extremal values are approached as powers of $1/\ln(\mu_Q/T)$. With a Dirichlet condition on the scalar source, the same solutions describe a non-conformal theory with scale $\Lambda$, whose charged branes exist only below $T_{\max}(\mu_Q)$, which falls from $0.194\Lambda$ at zero density to zero at $\mu_Q=0.506\Lambda$. This boundary is a diffusive instability where the charge susceptibility diverges at nonzero density, and the bulk viscosity violates Buchel's bound at all densities. Quasinormal modes with the normalizable large-radius condition reproduce its hydrodynamics.

hep-th.title: Holographic theory of non-invertible gravitational anomalies
hep-th.author: Xiao-Gang Wen
hep-th.abstract: We review a many-body formulation of gravitational anomalies as obstructions to realizing the complete low-energy data by a local {\it bosonic} lattice quantum system of the same dimension. In this formulation, an anomalous theory can be realized at the boundary of a gapped {\it bosonic} lattice bulk, whose topological order gives a one-to-one classification of the anomaly. An invertible bulk reproduces conventional anomaly inflow; a bulk with non-trivial topological excitations yields a non-invertible generalization. To describe the holographic theory of anomalies, we explain the distinction between uniquely defined topological order and many versions of topological quantum field theory and discuss the boundary-to-bulk map. As an application of the holographic theory of anomalies, we describe morphisms between local quantum theories (such as quantum field theories). These morphisms are built from a bulk domain wall and an invertible boundary junction, which give rise to a sandwich picture. Chiral boson/fermion theory, Laughlin edges, and boundaries of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ higher gauge theory with bosonic or fermionic point-like excitations illustrate the different kinds of information about non-invertible anomalies contained in transport coefficients, superselection sectors, and condensation data. In particular, a fermionic theory can be viewed as a theory with a particular non-invertible gravitational anomaly. Those examples also reveal that {\it symmetry $\sim$ gravitational anomaly $\sim$ topological order in one higher dimension}.

hep-th.title: Rank polarization and dynamical autonomy in a projective rotor model
hep-th.author: Shannon Wang, David Wang
hep-th.abstract: We study how a higher-rank classical collective order parameter can select one dominant projective eigenline and, in a $p=2$ realization, support a dynamically autonomous low-energy director sector. In a fully connected projective-rotor model, the collective second moment is a positive semidefinite tensor $T$ of fixed trace. Conventional projective ordering drives its effective rank toward one, selecting a single dominant eigenline. Rank polarization alone, however, does not determine dynamical autonomy: extrinsic-curvature criteria depend on the chosen state-space metric, and the equilibrium tensor does not determine the transverse free-energy Hessian. A two-harmonic model makes this logical independence explicit by producing families with identical $T$ and $r_{\rm eff}$ but different transverse quadratic forms. We then construct rotationally invariant locking interactions that leave a prescribed ordered tensor exactly fixed while increasing every non-Goldstone restoring coefficient as $\Theta(\lambda)$ within a globally controlled stable regime. For a phenomenological inertial realization with a finite positive kinetic matrix, the lowest transverse normal-mode frequency grows as $\Theta(\lambda^{1/2})$; more generally, the low-frequency transverse susceptibility is suppressed as $O(\lambda^{-1})$, including in overdamped dynamics. The construction therefore proves that spectral selection and infrared transverse suppression are independent data. For $p>2$ the selected eigenline has a $(p-1)$-dimensional director manifold; the one-dimensional Goldstone sector used in the dynamical construction is specific to $p=2$. Promoting the selected internal eigenline to a physical clock requires additional soldering and integrability structure.

hep-th.title: Phase transitions and quasinormal modes of Euler-Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes
hep-th.author: Yi-Qi Chen, De-Cheng Zou, Ming Zhang, Xufen Zhang, Bo Liu, Rui-Hong Yue
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we study phase transitions and scalar quasinormal modes(QNMs) of magnetically charged Euler--Heisenberg-dilaton AdS black holes in the extended phase space. We classify the horizon structures for all three signs of the EH coupling and derive the extended first law when the pressure and coupling are varied. For negative coupling, the physical branch exhibits a Van der Waals-like small/large black-hole transition. Using the improved asymptotic iteration method, we find two separated QNM trajectories below the critical pressure, whereas they merge into one continuous curve at the critical point. The GHS limit and the positive couplings considered here do not produce a finite-radius critical point.

hep-th.title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
hep-th.author: Andrea Cipriani
hep-th.abstract: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.

hep-th.title: New topological phase transitions in $κ$-deformed $ϕ^4$ lattice models
hep-th.author: Adith A, A. Bhagwat
hep-th.abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.

hep-th.title: Higher Dressing and Shift-Invariance in 4D Topological BF Theory
hep-th.author: J. François, L. Ravera
hep-th.abstract: A characteristic feature of topological field theories is the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. In four-dimensional BF theory with cosmological term, we make this feature manifest by exactly reducing the finite non-Abelian shift symmetry. We do so by identifying a higher dressing field, a 1-form compensating the shift, allowing to build from first principles the composite shift-invariant field $\boldsymbol{B}=B-\lambda^{-1}F$. In terms of this dressed field, the dynamics becomes algebraic and sets $\boldsymbol{B}=0$, directly exposing the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. This provides the first explicit instance of the higher-form Dressing Field Method.

hep-th.title: Area metric gravity à la Plebanski: connection, curvature and dynamics
hep-th.author: Bianca Dittrich
hep-th.abstract: Area metrics arise as effective description at intermediate scales in a number of approaches to quantum gravity, including string theory, holography and loop quantum gravity. Recently, it has been shown that area metric actions can be derived from the modified Plebanski framework on the linearized level. Surprisingly these actions avoid extra poles in the propagator for the effective length dynamics, and hence constitute interesting deformations of linearized Einstein gravity. To be able to study whether this property persist for the full theory, we construct here non-linear area metric dynamics from modified Plebanski actions. We provide the geometric tools for area metrics that do not rely on perturbation theory and allow a systematic construction and study of general non-linear area metric actions: an algorithm that extracts a length metric from an area metric and a connection on two-forms that is uniquely determined by the area metric, together with its curvature and curvature invariants. We derive area metric actions from modified Plebanski actions in first and second order versions. We also find that area metric actions can be reformulated as Poincare gauge theories. We determine the effective length metric action, which on a flat background describes a graviton and a massive spin-two field with parity-violating couplings set by the Barbero--Immirzi parameter. Additionally we discuss cosmological backgrounds and the role of the matter coupling, which together open the way to cosmological applications.

hep-th.title: From Lyapunov Growth to Weak Quantum Chaos
hep-th.author: Sašo Grozdanov, Tomaž Prosen
hep-th.abstract: Local out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) measure the growth of initially small commutators. For bounded local operators, this growth ends when the local commutator becomes of order one, but in an extended system the region over which it is large can continue to expand. We study this spatial proliferation using three related observables: the local squared commutator $C_r(t)$, its spatial sum $\bar C(t) = \sum_r C_r(t)$, and the symmetrically regularised connected dOTOC $D(t)$ of two extensive observables. We show that Lieb--Robinson locality gives $\bar C(t) \lesssim t^d$. We then prove that, in a Gibbs state with uniform exponential clustering, the full dOTOC obeys the same bound, $D(t) \lesssim t^d$, improving our earlier suboptimal $t^{3d}$ bound. We illustrate these results in two quantum many-body systems: a Brownian coupled-cluster model and a finite-temperature SYK chain. In both cases, an exact disorder symmetry relates $D(t)$ to $\bar C(t)$ and allows us to follow the same extensive observable from the pre-scrambling Lyapunov regime into the post-scrambling growth associated with an expanding saturated region. This late-time power-law growth is the concrete realisation of the weak quantum chaos introduced in our earlier work.

hep-th.title: Microscopic entropy of regular BTZ black holes in 3d Lovelock gravity at all orders
hep-th.author: Hikmet Özşahin
hep-th.abstract: We give a microscopic derivation of the semi-classical entropy of the black holes of 3d Lovelock gravity with an infinite tower of regularized Lovelock corrections, which include the regular BTZ black holes found recently. Working in the mini-superspace formalism, we show that the reduced action and its boundary term can be obtained in closed form at all orders in terms of the generating function of the couplings. Assuming the ground state is described by the soliton obtained from the static black hole by a double Wick rotation, we compute the soliton mass and reproduce the semi-classical entropy from the Cardy formula without central charges for arbitrary couplings. We then extend the mini-superspace to stationary configurations, compute the mass and the angular momentum of the rotating black holes obtained by a boost, and verify the Cardy formula in the presence of rotation.

hep-th.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
hep-th.author: Vladan Djukić, Mihailo Čubrović
hep-th.abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.

hep-th.title: Symmetric Dual Breather Modes as a Dynamic Origin of Tiny Particle Masses
hep-th.author: Yoritaka Iwata, Yasuhiro Takei
hep-th.abstract: Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) is conventionally understood through static vacuum selection in low-energy approximations. However, the nonperturbative dynamical pathways connecting symmetric configurations to asymmetric states remain an open question. In this paper, we propose an operator-theoretic framework that characterizes $Z_{2}$ symmetry breaking in scalar field theory through spectral branching. Specifically, we identify an effective invariant manifold of the nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation termed the "symmetric dual breather mode," whose phase-space geometry is traced using a $t$-dependent finite-dimensional representation. Our analysis demonstrates that static SSB represents merely a small-amplitude limit ($A \ll \phi_{v1}$). As the amplitude increases into the heteroclinic regime ($A > \phi_{v1}$), the field dynamically overflows the central barrier, yielding a vanishing time-averaged order parameter ($\langle \phi \rangle = 0$) and driving a geometric curvature cancellation ($\langle V''(\phi) \rangle_{t} \to 0$). Governed by a universal scaling function $\mathfrak{F}(y)$, the logarithmic period divergence near the heteroclinic boundary naturally generates sub-eV effective mass scales without fine-tuning bare parameters. Furthermore, this dynamic barrier overflow naturally favors Majorana-like self-conjugate states over Dirac-type states. Additionally, nonlinear phase interference along the heteroclinic channel induces asymmetric phase-space contraction, decoupling the right-handed mode and dynamically giving rise to the left-handed Weyl equation. These results bridge nonperturbative wave dynamics, topological mass suppression, chiral selection, and the dynamic origin of active neutrino masses.

hep-th.title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
hep-th.author: ZiHao Liu, Mei Huang
hep-th.abstract: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

hep-th.title: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
hep-th.author: Wei Fan, Xiao Yan Chew
hep-th.abstract: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.

hep-th.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
hep-th.author: Peter D. Jarvis, Jean Thierry-Mieg
hep-th.abstract: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).

hep-th.title: Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
hep-th.author: Wentao Zeng, Yifan He, Xian Wu
hep-th.abstract: We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.

hep-th.title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
hep-th.author: Guangshang Chen, Jianpeng Dai, Yang Xiao
hep-th.abstract: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

hep-th.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
hep-th.author: Paul H Frampton
hep-th.abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

hep-th.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
hep-th.author: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal, Mianqi Wang, Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Sudip Chakraborty, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Rama Govindarajan, Akshit Goyal, Jonathan J. Heckman, Yasir Iqbal, Divya Jaganathan, Saumav Kapoor, Andreas Karch, Pushkar Khandare, Sandeep Krishna, Anupam Kundu, Alok Laddha, Tongyan Lin, Swarnendu Maity, Nilmani Mathur, Shani Nadir Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Abhijeet Mishra, Vidur Niranjan, Abhishodh Prakash, Pratik Rath, Durbar Roy, Debargha Sarkar, Srikanth Sastry, Gary Shiu, Aninda Sinha, Thomas Van Riet, Praneeth Netrapalli, Suvrat Raju
hep-th.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

hep-th.title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
hep-th.author: Marta Bucca, Akash Jain, Márk Mezei, Alexey Milekhin
hep-th.abstract: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.

hep-th.title: Metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black holes
hep-th.author: Yu Shi, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Weike Deng, Sheng Long
hep-th.abstract: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.

hep-th.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
hep-th.author: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh
hep-th.abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theoris, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$.
